articles.summary: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu struck south coastal Andhra Pradesh, resulting in two fatalities after buildings collapsed in Bapatla district. Prakhar Jain of the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority stated that over 12,000 people sought shelter in rehabilitation facilities. The India Meteorological Department reported maximum sustained winds of 110 to 120 kilometers per hour during landfall near Ongole, causing widespread crop destruction and transport disruptions.
articles.description: Cyclone brings heavy rain to Prakasam and Palnadu districts; wind speed during landfall was 110-120 kmph, says IMD; 12,230 people are in rehabilitation centres in Guntur, Bapatla, and Palnadu districts; preliminary reports estimate losses of ₹344 crore

articles.headline: Israeli political deadlock persists as parliamentary majority remains elusive for blocs
articles.title: Israel political deadlock leaves Netanyahu’s future hanging in the balance
articles.summary: Israel faces political uncertainty as election certification approaches with neither major political bloc securing a parliamentary majority in the 120-seat Knesset. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu secured 53 seats, while opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot obtained 48 seats. Opposition figures plan to form a national emergency government, though potential alliances with Arab-led lists or ultra-Orthodox factions remain uncertain ahead of the November 10 swearing-in ceremony.
articles.description: With neither bloc near a majority, Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties hold the key to Israel’s next government..

articles.headline: Volodymyr Zelenskyy hopes upcoming Abu Dhabi talks will lead to trilateral meeting
articles.title: Ukraine’s Zelenskyy hopes Abu Dhabi talks will open path to Putin meeting
articles.summary: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed optimism that upcoming United States-mediated discussions in Abu Dhabi will pave the way for a trilateral meeting involving Russian President Vladimir Putin. Speaking in Berlin alongside German Chancellor Friedrich Merz, Zelenskyy highlighted the diplomatic efforts scheduled for November 10 and 11. Meanwhile, European officials are holding separate talks in Brussels regarding post-war security architecture and ongoing financial support for Ukraine.
articles.description: Ukrainian president meets German chancellor in Berlin, who says Russia is yet to engage seriously in peace efforts.

articles.headline: Republicans scramble in final push ahead of midterm elections
articles.title: Trump's Republicans scramble to stop Democratic midterms wave
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump and Republican candidates made a final push on November 1, 2026, ahead of November 3 midterm elections where Democrats are projected to take control of the House. According to NBC News, 60 percent of Americans disapprove of Trump's performance amid inflation and an eight-month conflict with Iran. Campaigns saw roughly 11 billion dollars spent on advertising, with heavy donations from figures like Elon Musk. High-stakes contests and early voting by 54 million citizens reflect intense national political division.
articles.description: While Tuesday is election day, early voting has already seen a record 54 million people cast ballots around the country, reflecting the intense political fervour

articles.headline: Syrian security forces foil alleged Hezbollah plot targeting Homs oil refinery
articles.title: Syria says it foiled Hezbollah plot to target Homs oil refinery
articles.summary: Syrian security forces arrested members of a cell linked to Lebanon’s Hezbollah group for planning an attack on the Homs refinery. Hezbollah denied involvement, stating it maintains no presence in Syria. Separately, Syrian authorities announced arrests of suspected ISIL members in Deir Az Zor following recent infrastructure attacks across the country, according to state media reports.
articles.description: Hezbollah denies the Syrian accusations, reiterating that it does not have any presence on Syrian territory.

articles.headline: US midterm campaign spending reaches record twelve billion dollars amid cost concerns
articles.title: How US midterms have cost a record $12bn as cost of living soars
articles.summary: Candidates and outside political groups have spent nearly twelve billion dollars on the United States midterm elections, according to OpenSecrets. Critics argue that unregulated super PAC funding gives wealthy donors excessive influence during an election cycle dominated by affordability issues. Meanwhile, the lobbying group American Israel Public Affairs Committee has faced scrutiny for channeling millions through shell political action committees.
articles.description: Candidates, donors and super PACs are spending more than ever on political campaigns.

articles.headline: Tata Motors completes acquisition of Iveco Group in multibillion-euro deal
articles.title: Tata-Iveco €3.8-bn deal turns global ambition into reality; eyes cross-market expansion
articles.summary: Tata Motors completed its €3.8-billion acquisition of Iveco Group NV, creating a combined commercial vehicle enterprise with presence in over 130 countries. Tata Sons Chairman N Chandrasekaran announced that the merged entity will pursue cross-market expansion, introducing Iveco products in India and Tata vehicles in international markets supported by 27 manufacturing facilities.
articles.description: The road ahead is to move forward with a shared ambition of Tata Motors and Iveco Group NV to create a stronger, more innovative and more resilient commercial mobility enterprise

articles.headline: Israeli opposition leaders back Gadi Eisenkot to replace Benjamin Netanyahu
articles.title: Israel’s opposition leaders back Eisenkot to oust Netanyahu
articles.summary: Five opposition party leaders agreed to support former military chief Gadi Eisenkot for prime minister during a meeting in Herzliya. The bloc aims to rapidly replace Benjamin Netanyahu’s government before President Isaac Herzog begins coalition consultations. However, the opposition remains divided regarding potential alliances with Arab-led parties, whose combined nineteen seats could prove decisive in the one hundred twenty seat Knesset.
articles.description: Opposition promises to form a government quickly but remains split over whether to ally with Arab-led parties.

articles.headline: Delhi booth-level officers instructed to seek additional citizenship proof
articles.title: Delhi SIR: Aadhaar alone not enough, BLOs asked to seek ‘citizenship proof’ from voters
articles.summary: Booth-level officers across constituencies in the national capital are facing renewed scrutiny during the special intensive revision of electoral rolls. Officials reported being directed to collect further documents from electors who previously submitted only Aadhaar cards to establish citizenship, despite more than 94% of flagged cases having been marked for final rolls by the Delhi Chief Electoral Officer.
articles.description: Regarding those electors flagged for ‘no mapping’ notices, several BLOs claim that Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) were directing them to revisit voters and seek additional documents to establish that they were not ‘Bangladeshi’ or ‘Rohingya’

articles.headline: Black Sea commercial shipping targeted as Russia and Ukraine escalate attacks
articles.title: Global food security is under threat
articles.summary: Escalating drone strikes by Russia and Ukraine on commercial vessels and port infrastructure in the Black Sea and Danube region have severely disrupted global grain exports and threatened food security. The attacks have knocked out significant export capacities for both nations, driving up international wheat futures and raising diplomatic tensions with NATO member states over maritime security.
articles.description: Attacks on grain shipments from Russia and Ukraine may drive up food prices, hitting import-dependent countries hardest.

articles.headline: Supreme Court rules foreign divorce decrees based on marriage breakdown invalid
articles.title: Divorce granted by foreign court on ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage not legal: SC
articles.summary: The Supreme Court held that foreign divorce decrees granted on the ground of irretrievable breakdown of marriage are not legal in India. Justices Prashant Kumar Mishra and Shree Chandrashekhar issued the ruling while dismissing a man's plea against bigamy and criminal conspiracy charges lodged by his first wife under the Indian Penal Code.
articles.description: In our view, the foreign divorce decree was passed in contravention of the existing matrimonial law in India and on a ground that is not even recognised statutorily, the bench said

articles.headline: Anthropic warns artificial intelligence advancement could outpace human safety controls
articles.title: Anthropic warns AI could outpace human control in developing successor models
articles.summary: Artificial intelligence developer Anthropic warned in a regulatory filing that recursive self-improvement could accelerate the creation of advanced systems faster than safety safeguards can be implemented. The company reported that its Claude model wrote over 90% of code in September and achieved a 90% success rate on engineering benchmarks, raising concerns about maintaining adequate human supervision.
articles.description: The Claude maker says future models may soon drive faster AI progress, potentially outpacing safety, alignment and security measures

articles.headline: Trump administration plans to remove South Africa and Rwanda from trade agreement
articles.title: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump notified Congress of his plan to exclude South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act beginning January 1, 2027. United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated that annual reviews revealed both countries engaged in practices violating program requirements. Washington cited trade barriers, security concerns, and human rights issues as the primary reasons for the upcoming terminations.
articles.description: The move comes barely a week after Rwanda's defence ministry was hit with sanctions by the US Treasury.

articles.headline: Russian airstrikes on Komyshuvakha aid centre kill 24 people
articles.title: Russian bombing kills 31 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
articles.summary: At least 24 people were killed after Russian aerial bombs struck a humanitarian aid distribution centre located inside a school in the southern Zaporizhzhia region village of Komyshuvakha. According to Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and regional head Mykhailo Semikin, the attack injured five people and left 27 missing. Rescue operations were repeatedly halted due to ongoing drone activity.
articles.description: Officials say at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit a southern Ukrainian village in what the president calls an "utterly horrific" attack.

articles.headline: Iran outlines five conditions for regional security amidst ongoing diplomatic mediation
articles.title: Iran commander sets out five conditions for regional security
articles.summary: Major-General Ali Abdollahi presented a five-point roadmap demanding an end to hostilities, the lifting of sanctions, and recognition of sovereignty over the Strait of Hormuz. Meanwhile, Qatari mediators engaged in talks in Tehran to restart negotiations between Iran and the United States, following recent military strikes and drone incidents near Qeshm Island involving American and Iranian forces.
articles.description: Mediator Qatar says US and Iran are studying proposals to resume negotiations and that it was 'hopeful' of an agreement.

articles.headline: Kremlin confirms US-mediated Russia-Ukraine peace talks in Abu Dhabi
articles.title: Kremlin confirms Ukraine-U.S. talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10-11
articles.summary: The Kremlin announced on November 3, 2026, that Russian and Ukrainian delegations will participate in United States-mediated trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi on November 10 and 11. President Vladimir Putin selected aide Vladimir Medinsky to lead the Russian team. Washington continues pushing for a resolution to the four-year conflict following previous diplomatic efforts.
articles.description: U.S. President Donald Trump's special envoy Steve Witkoff earlier announced the meeting will take place on November 10-11

articles.headline: Cyberattack disrupts supermarkets across Europe
articles.title: Cyberattack disrupts supermarkets across Europe
articles.description: Cyberattack disrupts supermarkets across Europe

articles.headline: Black Sea vessel attacks escalate tensions and threaten global food security
articles.title: Grain under fire: Russian, Ukrainian Black Sea attacks threaten food supply
articles.summary: Naval and aerial drones struck the Liberian-flagged freighter Contship Jet Monrovia off Bulgaria on October 28, sinking the ship though all 18 crew members survived. Kyiv attributed the attack to Russian forces aiming to disrupt Ukrainian agricultural exports. The European Union condemned the maritime strikes, noting that ongoing violence significantly impacts global wheat prices and supplies.
articles.description: Renewed strikes on Black Sea shipping imperil grain exports, drive up food prices and deepen global food insecurity.

articles.headline: United States urges Venezuela to release remaining political prisoners
articles.title: US urges Venezuela to release remaining political prisoners
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio met Venezuelan counterpart Oliver Blanco on Monday to demand the immediate release of 322 remaining political prisoners. Opposition figures continue advocating for rapid democratic reforms following Nicolás Maduro's removal in January. The State Department emphasized ongoing support for Donald Trump's structured transition plan and electoral infrastructure updates.
articles.description: The US secretary of state also discusses laying the groundwork for 'free, fair, and credible elections'.

articles.headline: Iran displays billboards in Tehran threatening US President Trump
articles.title: Iran unveils huge billboard with threat against Donald Trump’s life
articles.summary: Iran displayed massive billboards across Tehran on Tuesday depicting threats against United States President Donald Trump. The public displays featured hostile imagery and called for revenge following previous attacks, coinciding with diplomatic tensions and legislative elections taking place in the United States while mediation efforts continued.
articles.description: We will kill Trump, read the billboard towering over the busy Enghelab Square in Tehran

articles.headline: World Bank reports nearly 500 million people lifted out of poverty
articles.title: How India pulled 500 million people out of poverty as inequality deepens
articles.summary: A new World Bank report revealed that India lifted 496 million people out of extreme poverty between 2011 and 2023, reducing the national rate from 27 percent to 2.6 percent. Authors attributed the decline to strong consumption growth, rising female employment, and expanded social welfare programs. Despite this historic progress, income inequality across the country remains exceptionally high.
articles.description: India's extreme poverty declined from 27.1 percent to 2.6 percent between 2011 and 2023, according to the World Bank.

articles.headline: Darius Khambata criticises Tata Sons chairman reappointment decision
articles.title: Chandra’s reappointment has sullied Tata Sons’ image: Darius Khambata
articles.summary: Outgoing Tata Trusts board member Darius Khambata has resigned, stating that the decision to grant N. Chandrasekaran a third term as Tata Sons chairman has damaged the company's reputation. Khambata expressed his concerns in a letter to Tata Trusts chairman Noel Tata, highlighting internal divisions regarding share listings and fiduciary duties.
articles.description: ‘The sad events of September 17, 2026, a day that will live in infamy, have sullied Tata Sons’ reputation and imperilled the image of corporate India. No amount of spin doctoring can mask what happened,’ said the outgoing Tata Trusts board member

articles.headline: US forces strike Iran island as diplomatic talks continue
articles.title: US hits Qeshm Island, Pezeshkian signals more diplomacy: Iran war latest
articles.summary: United States forces launched defensive strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island on Monday, according to officials, amid ongoing mediation efforts led by Qatar. The military action followed a series of regional escalations and diplomatic discussions involving Iranian and international representatives as leaders assessed potential pathways toward ending the ongoing conflict between the two nations.
articles.description: With the first US attack on Qeshm Island since June, Iran and the US are on parallel tracks towards both peace and war.

articles.headline: US conducts series of ‘defensive strikes’ against Iran
articles.title: US conducts series of ‘defensive strikes’ against Iran
articles.description: The US has carried out a series of ‘defensive strikes’ on Iranian locations near Hormuz, with explosions heard on Qeshm.

articles.headline: Russian strikes hit Ukrainian hospital and energy sites
articles.title: At least 73 injured as Russia bombs Ukrainian hospital and power plants
articles.summary: Russian forces launched a massive aerial bombardment targeting energy infrastructure and a clinical hospital in Kharkiv, injuring at least 73 people on Monday night. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy reported extensive damage across multiple regions, while international officials prepared for upcoming diplomatic discussions regarding security arrangements.
articles.description: Medical facility was struck by Russian ballistic missiles and aerial bombs overnight.

articles.headline: Iran and Saudi Arabia continue talks amid intensifying Yemen fighting
articles.title: Iran's Foreign Minister says talks with Saudi Arabia are ongoing; Yemen fighting intensifies
articles.summary: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi announced ongoing talks with Saudi Arabia on November 3, 2026, aimed at establishing regional security without foreign military involvement. The diplomatic contacts follow high-level meetings in Tehran and escalated Houthi attacks on Saudi oil facilities, airports, and shipping routes amid the ongoing civil war in Yemen.
articles.description: Riyadh said the talks are intended to open negotiating channels to “prevent ‌the return of military escalation,” ​as fighting between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Iran-aligned Houthis had intensified ⁠in recent weeks

articles.headline: Cyclone Murasu makes landfall on India eastern coast
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu makes landfall on India’s eastern coast
articles.summary: Severe cyclonic storm Murasu made landfall near Ongole in Andhra Pradesh on Tuesday, uprooting trees and flooding low-lying areas. The India Meteorological Department warned of heavy rainfall across the region, while authorities evacuated thousands of residents following an earlier storm that struck the area days prior.
articles.description: Severe cyclonic storm uproots trees and downs power lines, days after another cyclone battered the same region.

articles.headline: Saudi Arabia postpones 2027 Asian Cup football tournament over safety
articles.title: 2027 Asian Cup football tournament in Saudi Arabia postponed over safety
articles.summary: The Asian Football Confederation postponed the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia from January until December 2027 due to regional security concerns and logistical complexities. The tournament will now run from December 23, 2027, to January 21, 2028, pending FIFA approval, following recent Houthi attacks that disrupted multiple sporting events across the host nation.
articles.description: A number of sports events in Saudi Arabia have been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following Houthi attacks on the country

articles.headline: Indian seafarer killed and 13 rescued after ship attack near Oman
articles.title: Indian seafarer killed in attack on ship near Oman; 13 others rescued: MEA
articles.summary: An Indian sailor was killed and 13 others were rescued following an attack on the commercial vessel MSV Al Jusufi near Limah in Oman on November 2, 2026. The Ministry of External Affairs stated the ship was struck by an aerial object, prompting India to urge immediate de-escalation and safe navigation in regional international waterways.
articles.description: The deceased seafarer was identified as Gandhar Nahim Ajij from Gujarat; India reiterates call for immediate de-escalation of tensions in the region

articles.headline: Child dies from measles in rural northern New York
articles.title: Child dies of measles in New York's first such death in 30 years
articles.summary: A child in Lewis County has died from measles in New York's first fatality from the viral disease in 30 years, state officials announced on November 2, 2026. Governor Kathy Hochul attributed the tragedy to declining vaccination rates below necessary coverage thresholds, prompting an earlier disaster emergency declaration to expand vaccine administration access.
articles.description: The U.S. stopped the domestic spread of measles in 2000 by maintaining high vaccination rates, but they have fallen in recent years to below the 95% coverage needed to prevent outbreaks of the viral disease

articles.headline: Asian Cup postponed in Saudi Arabia following deadly regional attacks
articles.title: Asian Cup postponed in wake of attacks on Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: The Asian Football Confederation has postponed the 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia to December 2027 following deadly attacks and travel disruptions in the region. Originally set for January, the rescheduling prevents several Premier League players from missing club matches, while other high-profile sports events in the host country have also been cancelled or delayed.
articles.description: The 2027 Asian Cup in Saudi Arabia is postponed because of a series of deadly attacks on the host country.

articles.headline: Palestinian citizens face political fallout after Israeli election gains
articles.title: Palestine weekly: Election deadlock meets West Bank sieges, Gaza killings
articles.summary: Following a record election performance by Arab-led parties winning 19 seats, Palestinian communities across Israel and the occupied West Bank experienced severe political delegitimisation, military sieges, and ongoing violence. According to the United Nations and local officials, operations in Hebron displaced thousands and caused significant economic losses before the army withdrew on November 2, while conflict-related casualties in Gaza continued to mount amid intensified regional instability.
articles.description: As Israel grapples with an inconclusive election, Palestinians face West Bank closures and Gaza killings.

articles.headline: Russian strikes on Zaporizhzhia village kill 26 people following truce expiration
articles.title: Russia-Ukraine war: Strikes on a school by Russia kills 26, derailing hopes of progress toward peace
articles.summary: Ukrainian officials stated that Russian strikes on a Zaporizhzhia village school distributing humanitarian aid killed at least 26 people on November 2, 2026. The attack followed the expiry of a Kherson ceasefire brokered by U.S. First Lady Melania Trump. Acting regional Governor Mykhailo Semikin confirmed casualties included rescuers and police officers as U.S.-led talks approach.
articles.description: Russia resumed its strikes on the southern region of Kherson after the end of a ceasefire in the area, the longest truce in the war raging between the neighbours since Russia’s 2022 invasion, Kyiv said

articles.headline: Severe cyclone Murasu approaches Andhra Pradesh coast for landfall
articles.title: Severe Cyclone Murasu: Landfall commences near Ongole
articles.summary: The India Meteorological Department reported that severe cyclonic storm Murasu is approaching the coastline of Andhra Pradesh near Ongole. Landfall is expected before three in the morning on November 3, 2026. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority issued warnings for extremely heavy rainfall across multiple mandals in Prakasam district, amid gales reaching up to one hundred kilometers per hour.
articles.description: The landfall is happening close to Ongole, with gale-force winds of 100-110 kmph, gusting to 120 kmph; he same wind speed is likely to prevail till morning along and off the coast near the landfall point.

articles.headline: Democrats threaten Republican control of the US Senate ahead of midterm elections
articles.title: Republicans defend their bastions, as senate comes within reach of Democrats
articles.summary: As the United States approaches midterm elections, forecasts indicate that the Republican Party majority in the Senate is under threat from Democrats. The party currently holds a 53 to 47 majority with thirty-five seats contested this year, including seven toss-up seats identified by the Cook Political Report across several states according to reports published on October twenty-ninth, 2026.
articles.description: The GOP has a 53–47 majority in the Senate currently, with 35 seats being contested this year. Of these, seven are “toss ups”, according to a non-partisan election analyser. These seats are in Iowa, Arkansas, Kansas, Maine, Michigan, Ohio and Texas. All of these – except Michigan – are seats which are currently held by Republicans

articles.headline: Russian air defenses intercept numerous drones following conclusion of regional truce
articles.title: Russia downs hundreds of drones after Ukraine truce ends
articles.summary: Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin reported that Russian air defenses intercepted nearly 500 drones targeting the capital on November 3, 2026. The escalation followed the expiration of a Kherson region truce on November 1. Concurrently, strikes across Ukraine killed 26 people, triggered Polish air defenses, and disrupted regional medical and critical infrastructure as U.S.-led talks loom.
articles.description: The attacks followed a rare pause in the fighting between Russia and Ukraine in the southern Ukrainian region of Kherson, which ended November 1

articles.headline: Former Maldives foreign minister Abdulla Shahid arrested on abuse charges
articles.title: Former Maldives Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid arrested on child sexual abuse charges
articles.summary: Police in the Maldives arrested former Foreign Minister Abdulla Shahid late Monday following a court order concerning child sexual abuse allegations. Local media reported that the prominent opposition politician has denied the charges. The arrest holds significance as the former United Nations General Assembly president is a presidential aspirant for the Maldivian Democratic Party in the upcoming elections.
articles.description: The arrest assumes significance as Mr. Shahid is among the prominent presidential aspirants within the main opposition Maldivian Democratic Party (MDP) for the island nation’s 2028 elections

articles.headline: Texas Senate candidates Paxton and Talarico make final appeals
articles.title: Texas Senate candidates Paxton and Talarico make final appeals
articles.description: Texas Senate candidates Ken Paxton (R) and James Talarico (D) made their last appearances before Tuesday’s election.

articles.headline: Israeli military attacks across Gaza leave multiple Palestinians dead and injured
articles.title: Israeli forces kill four in Gaza as fifth Palestinian dies of wounds
articles.summary: Medical sources and media reports stated that Israeli forces killed at least four Palestinians in attacks across Gaza, while a fifth person died from previous wounds. The Palestinian Ministry of Health reported that ongoing operations have killed at least 74,609 people. Meanwhile, Board of Peace high representative Nickolay Mladenov arrived in Israel to discuss reconstruction and winter shelter.
articles.description: Nearly 1,600 Palestinians have been killed in Gaza since a US-brokered 'ceasefire' took effect in October last year.

articles.headline: American voters head to the polls amid economic concerns and low approval ratings
articles.title: Americans head to the polls for elections that could define Trump's closing chapter
articles.summary: Voters across the United States are heading to the polls on Tuesday for midterm elections that will determine control of Congress. Public concern centers on the high cost of living, inflation, and soaring fuel prices driven by aggressive tariffs and an ongoing war with Iran. According to polls, President Donald Trump faces low approval ratings, though political analysts note this does not necessarily translate to a sweeping victory for the Democratic Party.
articles.description: The midterms will shape Congress for the last years of his presidency, writes Sarah Smith, but they are also a test of what politics may look like without him.

articles.headline: US midterms test Republican redistricting strategies in Texas and beyond
articles.title: US midterms present a test for Republican redistricting in Texas and beyond
articles.summary: Republican state legislatures implemented rare mid-decade redistricting in Texas and other states ahead of midterm elections to secure potential congressional gains. Critics argue the new boundaries dilute minority voting power by altering traditional districts, while defenders maintain the changes reflect shifting voter trends. Approximately thirty-five million voters nationwide are casting ballots within newly redrawn political boundaries for this election cycle.
articles.description: Partisan redistricting has transformed elections for Black voters in Houston as Democrats seek new pathways to victory.

articles.headline: Delhi air quality plunges to very poor category as stage two GRAP invoked
articles.title: Air quality of Delhi slips to ‘very poor’ for first time this winter, Stage 2 of GRAP invoked
articles.summary: Air quality in the national capital deteriorated sharply, prompting the implementation of Stage-II of the Graded Response Action Plan across the National Capital Region on Monday. The air quality index reached 324, driven by unfavourable meteorological conditions according to forecasts from the India Meteorological Department. Authorities directed regional governments to increase parking fees and stagger office timings to curb rising pollution levels.
articles.description: AQI of Delhi stood at 324 (very poor) at 4 p.m. on November 2, up from 261 (poor) a day earlier; NCR State governments to enhance vehicle parking fees to discourage use of private vehicles, staggered timings to be introduced for public offices and municipal bodies; Delhi Metro to run 20 more trips on weekdays

articles.headline: Israeli forces arrest Al Jazeera correspondent Montaser Nassar in West Bank
articles.title: Israeli forces release Al Jazeera journalist in occupied West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli soldiers detained Al Jazeera Arabic correspondent Montaser Nassar during a raid on his home in Dura, near Hebron, on Tuesday. Video footage showed him blindfolded and handcuffed before being led into a military vehicle alongside at least 12 other Palestinians. According to sources, all detainees were taken to an undisclosed location following the operation in the occupied West Bank.
articles.description: Al Jazeera correspondent Montaser Nassar released hours after being arrested at his home in Dura, near Hebron.

articles.headline: Delhi air quality remains very poor with severe pollution in parts
articles.title: Parts of Delhi reel under ‘severe’ level air pollution
articles.summary: Delhi maintained a very poor air quality category on November 3, 2026, with specific areas like Rohini, Punjabi Bagh, and Narela recording severe pollution levels. According to Central Pollution Control Board data, the 24-hour average Air Quality Index reached 330 at 8 a.m. Meteorological factors and seasonal stubble burning continue to worsen regional air conditions across northern India.
articles.description: The 24-hour average Air Quality Index (AQI) of Delhi was 330 (very poor) at 8 a.m. on November 3, 2026, as per Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB) data

articles.headline: Israeli soldiers arrest Al Jazeera journalist in Hebron raids
articles.title: Israeli soldiers arrest Al Jazeera journalist in Hebron raids
articles.description: Israeli soldiers blindfolded, handcuffed and arrested Al Jazeera correspondent Montaser Nassar during a raid on his home

articles.headline: United States military carries out defensive strikes against Iranian targets in Strait of Hormuz
articles.title: U.S. has conducted defensive strikes on some Iranian targets in Strait of Hormuz: official ahead of midterm elections
articles.summary: American forces executed limited defensive strikes on Monday, November 2, 2026, targeting Iranian assets utilizing surface-to-air missiles near Qeshm Island. The operation occurred ahead of United States midterm elections, as Vice-President J.D. Vance expressed optimism regarding potential negotiated settlements. Meanwhile, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu reportedly lobbied for continued military action to aid domestic political objectives.
articles.description: Vice-President J.D. Vance told reporters that he just spoke to President Trump about talks with Iran and said that “the president and I both feel pretty good about the prospects for potentially coming to a negotiated settlement”

articles.headline: Indian Space Research Organisation successfully launches NVS-03 satellite
articles.title: Back to back GSLV successes help ISRO win back some pride
articles.summary: The Indian Space Research Organisation launched the NVS-03 satellite using the GSLV-F18 vehicle from Sriharikota on October 30, 2026. The successful deployment into a geosynchronous transfer orbit provided a positive milestone for Chairman V. Narayanan following previous mission setbacks.

articles.headline: Supreme Court declines administration request to segregate thousands of California mail ballots
articles.title: U.S. Supreme Court rejects Trump administration push to set aside thousands of California ballots
articles.summary: The Supreme Court declined on Monday, November 2, 2026, to intervene in a Republican administration request to set aside approximately 20,000 mail ballots in California flagged as potential non-citizens. Lower courts warned that segregating the documents before Tuesday midterm elections would disenfranchise legal voters and create severe logistical disruptions. Department of Justice attorneys acknowledged substantial error rates within their tracking data during the proceedings.
articles.description: Another federal judge ruled against the administration's efforts to make last-minute demands of California election officials, finding they violated the Constitution

articles.headline: Supreme Court stays Madras High Court order on Chidambaram temple management
articles.title: Supreme Court stays Madras HC order on Chidambaram temple
articles.summary: The Supreme Court froze the implementation of an October 30 order that established a Board of Management to administer the Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple in Tamil Nadu. Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi questioned whether state high courts hold parens patriae jurisdiction over places of worship beyond public temples, while hearing arguments from the Tamil Nadu government regarding alleged maladministration and property damage.
articles.description: Questions whether High Courts have parens patriae jurisdiction only over public temples and not places of worship of other faiths

articles.headline: Indian stock markets extend winning streak despite elevated volatility index
articles.title: VIX stays elevated despite five-day market rally as global risks keep investors on edge
articles.summary: Indian stock markets extended a winning streak for five consecutive sessions on Wednesday, November 4, 2026, as the Sensex gained 383 points to close at 77,301. Despite the recovery, the volatility index remained near 15 points due to global uncertainties, crude oil price fluctuations, and outcomes from United States midterm elections.
articles.description: Post the U.S. midterm elections, investor focus will shift to the U.S. administration’s next course of action on West Asia.

articles.headline: Death of TGSRTC conductor sparks protests across Khammam region
articles.title: TGSRTC conductor Pravalika’s death triggers protests across Khammam region; attempt-to-murder case altered to murder
articles.summary: Following the death of 24-year-old Telangana State Road Transport Corporation conductor G. Pravalika, employees staged widespread demonstrations and halted services across seven depots on November 4. Ms. Pravalika succumbed to injuries on November 3 after being pushed from a moving bus by a passenger on October 25. Police altered the initial attempt-to-murder case to murder under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita.

articles.headline: Kharge and Rijiju clash on social media over electoral and political issues
articles.title: Kharge asks Modi to face questions on ‘vote chori’, Rijiju spars with him on ‘dimaagi Naxals’
articles.summary: Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju clashed on the platform X on November 4 regarding the term dimaagi Naxals. Mr. Kharge urged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to address allegations of vote theft and electoral roll revisions by the Election Commission. Mr. Rijiju defended the term and categorized individuals who challenge the Indian Constitution and development projects.
articles.description: The Congress president said the Election Commission had made five U-turns on the SIR, while the Union Minister defined who he called ‘dimaagi Naxals’

articles.headline: Mumbai Police arrest three individuals in connection with cyber fraud racket
articles.title: Mumbai Police arrest three in Nagpur cyber fraud racket, establish links to 73 cases across India
articles.summary: Mumbai Police arrested three men from Nagpur on November 2 for operating a share trading investment fraud racket through a shell company named Grain Garden Delight Private Limited. Authorities linked the suspects to 73 cybercrime cases nationwide after seizing various bank documents, SIM cards, and electronic items. The operation was executed by the South Region Cyber Police following a technical investigation into fraudulent financial transactions.
articles.description: The investigation began after police traced ₹24.75 lakh from a share trading investment fraud case registered at the South Region Cyber Police Station to a current account opened in the company’s name at the Central Bank of India’s Jaripatka branch in Nagpur

articles.headline: Why is the western US still counting votes after election day?
articles.title: Why is the western US still counting votes after election day?
articles.description: Why is the western US still counting votes after election day?

articles.headline: Mother of slain Ghanaian teenager travels to America after receiving emergency visa
articles.title: Mother of Ghanaian boy killed in US 'wants justice' as she flies for funeral
articles.summary: Doris Adu Gyamfi left Ghana for the United States after President Donald Trump granted her an emergency visa to plan the funeral of her 15-year-old son, Javits Frimpong. The teenager was fatally shot on his way to school in the Bronx on Thursday morning. Police are currently searching for three teenage suspects captured on surveillance footage while investigating the tragic shooting incident.
articles.description: Police have not made any arrests and an investigation is ongoing as authorities search for three teenage boys.

articles.headline: Gold prices rise as dollar index drops to five-week low
articles.title: Gold shines as dollar slips to 5-week low, investors await U.S. midterm election results
articles.summary: Spot gold prices surged 3% to reach $4,041 per ounce on November 4 as the dollar index slipped to a five-week low of 101.3. Investors awaited United States midterm election results, which indicated sweeping Democratic victories in the House and Senate. Analysts attribute the price movement to initial market reactions, with upcoming trends depending on federal policies, crude prices, and geopolitical developments.
articles.description: A weaker dollar makes dollar-denominated assets like gold less expensive for consumers of other currencies, boosting demand for the yellow metal

articles.headline: Authorities open all seventy gates of Prakasam Barrage amid heavy rainfall
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: All 70 gates of Prakasam Barrage opened; 71,000 cusecs released into Krishna
articles.summary: The Water Resources Department opened all 70 gates of the Prakasam Barrage on November 4, 2026, discharging 71,000 cusecs of surplus water into the Krishna river. Officials suspended canal supplies to prevent flooding as Cyclone Murasu brought exceptionally heavy rainfall across central districts, with Palnadu district recording nearly 269.45 millimeters of rain.
articles.description: The inflows come largely from the Keesara, Munneru and Budameru streams after heavy rain in NTR district

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh election officials review polling arrangements ahead of local body votes
articles.title: Andhra Pradesh SEC reviews cyclone impact as MPTCs, ZPTCs go to polls today
articles.summary: State Election Commissioner Anil Chandra Punetha reviewed preparations on Wednesday for MPTC and ZPTC elections across Andhra Pradesh. Despite challenges from Cyclone Murasu, district collectors reported that rainfall had subsided and voting would proceed normally. State Election Secretary A. Mallikarjuna stated that 2.52 lakh officials were deployed for duty across 31,460 polling stations to accommodate approximately 2.61 crore eligible voters.
articles.description: Around 2.61 crore voters to exercise franchise at 31,460 polling stations; decisions on polling in cyclone-hit areas will be taken based on ground-level reports, says Punetha

articles.headline: United States encourages Venezuela to pursue phased democratic transition following high-level meeting
articles.title: US urges Venezuela to follow phased plan for democratic transition
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio met with Venezuelan Minister of Foreign Affairs Oliver Blanco on Monday to discuss a phased plan involving stabilization, economic recovery, and political reconciliation. The diplomatic engagement follows last year's abduction of former President Nicolas Maduro and recent oil agreements granting North American Blue Energy Partners significant extraction rights. Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado recently returned to organize upcoming electoral movements.
articles.description: This comes as leading opposition leader returns to Venezuela and hints at criticism of Trump administration.

articles.headline: Explosions rattle Qeshm Island as reports indicate American military action in Hormuz
articles.title: Explosions hit Iran’s Qeshm Island as US media report US strikes in Hormuz
articles.summary: Explosions occurred on Iran's Qeshm Island and in Bandar Lengeh on Monday, coinciding with reports from American media outlets that United States forces conducted defensive strikes in the Strait of Hormuz. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed responsibility for capturing two reconnaissance drones and destroying an MQ-9 drone. President Donald Trump subsequently minimized conflict prospects on social media ahead of Tuesday midterm elections.
articles.description: Several explosions heard on Qeshm Island and in Bandar Lengeh as US media report US military strikes in Hormuz.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh sounds alert as severe cyclonic storm Murasu approaches coast
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu nears A.P. coast, heavy rain alert issued
articles.summary: The Andhra Pradesh government issued alerts across five districts as severe cyclonic storm Murasu approached for landfall between Ongole and Nellore on November 2, 2026. The India Meteorological Department warned of very heavy rainfall and wind speeds reaching up to 120 kmph. Authorities deployed National Disaster Response Force teams, arranged electricity poles, and dispatched rescue personnel to manage potential disruptions.
articles.description: The India Meteorological Department (IMD) said the storm is likely to move with a “wind speed of 100 to 110 kmph (and) gusting up to 120 kmph between Nellore and Narasapur”.

articles.headline: Thousands displaced as homes are bulldozed in India’s Assam state
articles.title: Thousands displaced as homes are bulldozed in India’s Assam state
articles.description: Hundreds of homes have been bulldozed in the Dhubri district of Assam state in northeastern India.

articles.headline: Yemeni government forces advance into al-Jawf mountain range during ongoing offensive
articles.title: Yemeni government forces claim control of strategic al-Jawf mountain range
articles.summary: Yemeni government forces advanced into the al-Dahida mountain range in eastern al-Jawf province during their ongoing offensive against Houthi forces. Troops backed by air support seized weapons and military equipment from Houthi fortifications. Meanwhile, a Houthi ballistic missile strike hit a military training camp in al-Dhalea, killing eight people and wounding over fifteen, according to a military source.
articles.description: The advance on al-Dahida heights, a strategic highland, comes as fighting escalates in al-Dhalea, Lahij and Taiz.

articles.headline: Union Cabinet approves new VISTAR scheme to overhaul national statistical architecture
articles.title: Union Cabinet approves new VISTAR scheme to overhaul India’s statistical system
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved the Viksit Bharat Initiative for Statistical Transformation, Analytics and Research scheme with a budget of ₹4,371 crore for the period between 2026 and 2031. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation will execute the program through three components, which include conducting 59 surveys, providing funds to state governments, and undertaking the eighth Economic Census to gather granular data on unorganised sector establishments.
articles.description: The three-pronged scheme is aimed at strengthening data collecting, analysis, the incorporation of AI, as well as provide fresh data on the unorganised sector to make the overall GDP figure more accurate

articles.headline: Spanish Transport Minister resigns over train crash disasters
articles.title: Spanish Transport Minister resigns over train crash disasters
articles.description: Spanish Transport Minister resigns over train crash disasters

articles.headline: United States strikes Qeshm Island amid ongoing regional tensions and diplomatic discussions
articles.title: U.S. strikes Iran's Qeshm Island: report
articles.summary: The Wall Street Journal reported on Monday, November 2, 2026, that the United States military executed strikes on Iran's Qeshm Island following explosions noted by state media agency IRNA. The operation represents a continuation of limited, undisclosed actions distinct from full-scale military campaigns. President Donald Trump stated that a diplomatic agreement with Tehran remains possible and denied plans for post-election strikes.
articles.description: The Wall Street Journal added that strikes have been carried out on ‌a smaller scale and purposefully ​kept secret so as not to signal any intent ⁠of resuming its major military campaign against Iran

articles.headline: Israeli settlers erect new structures on Hebron rooftops threatening Palestinian businesses
articles.title: Hebron’s Israeli rooftop settlers threaten the city’s Palestinian identity
articles.summary: Israeli settlers placed mobile structures on commercial building rooftops in Hebron on October 29 to accommodate twenty new housing units. Palestinian business owners whose shops are situated below the structures expressed deep concern over losing their livelihoods and heritage. Activists note that this expansion undermines the Palestinian identity of the Old City, which has remained heavily restricted since the 1994 Ibrahimi Mosque massacre.
articles.description: Israeli settlers have expanded in Hebron's Old City, with Palestinian residents' presence under threat.

articles.headline: Maria Corina Machado returns to Venezuela after months in exile
articles.title: Venezuela's Opposition leader Machado returns after months in exile, as doubts over democracy deepen
articles.summary: Opposition leader Maria Corina Machado returned to Venezuela from exile on October 25, 2026, arriving in Lara to greet supporters. Her return follows the U.S. military ouster of former President Nicolas Maduro and acting President Delcy Rodriguez taking power. Machado and her allies have demanded a presidential election date, while U.S. officials emphasize prior economic stabilization.
articles.description: Acting President Delcy Rodriguez was initially supposed to serve only 90 days as acting president, but has remained in office and has made no move to call an election

articles.headline: Rahul Gandhi challenges Prime Minister Narendra Modi to open debate
articles.title: Rahul Gandhi challenges PM Modi to open debate on ‘foreign help’
articles.summary: Lok Sabha opposition leader Rahul Gandhi challenged Prime Minister Narendra Modi to an open debate following accusations that the opposition relies on foreign assistance to destabilise the country. Gandhi alleged on social media that Modi owes his position to foreign backing and financial support. Modi had previously criticized the opposition in Gujarat for obstructing national development and spreading rumors.
articles.description: Congress leader alleges that it was with ‘foreign help’ that Modi became PM; this comes after the Prime Minister accused the Opposition of taking foreign help to destabilise the country

articles.headline: Indian-American candidates secure victories during United States midterm elections
articles.title: US midterm election results 2026: Key Indian-origin winners
articles.summary: Several Indian-origin candidates secured congressional victories as Democrats made gains in the United States midterm elections on November 4, 2026. Suhas Subramanyam won in Virginia and Pia Dandiya won in Florida for the House of Representatives, whereas Republican candidate Vivek Ramaswamy lost the Ohio gubernatorial race to Democrat Amy Acton.
articles.description: Indian-Americans Suhas Subramanyam and Pia Dandiya won their seats in the US House of Representatives, while Vivek ‌Ramaswamy‌ was defeated in ⁠the ⁠race to become Ohio’s ‌next governor

articles.headline: European governments face persistent protests over living costs and political grievances
articles.title: Why are Europe’s governments struggling to respond to growing protests?
articles.summary: Demonstrations led largely by young people continue to sweep across at least eight European countries over grievances including school conditions, living costs, and political insecurity. Governments have struggled to respond effectively, often relying on security measures and public order responses rather than addressing underlying demands. Human rights organisations and United Nations officials have raised serious concerns regarding the use of police force against protesters.
articles.description: Protests intensify as governments prioritise security measures over addressing underlying social and economic concerns.

articles.headline: Mit Technology Review discusses data lineage for agentic enterprise security
articles.title: Securing the agentic enterprise with data lineage
articles.summary: As enterprises increasingly deploy autonomous artificial intelligence agents in daily operations, organizations face significant data visibility challenges when sensitive information spreads undetected across multiple complex workflows. According to a sponsored feature by Cyberhaven published in MIT Technology Review, traditional perimeter security models are no longer sufficient. Security teams must now establish comprehensive data lineage to manage governance and accountability across hybrid human and machine systems.
articles.description: A sales representative asks an AI agent for customer pricing, and the agent pulls data from multiple sources: restricted pricing systems, internal communications, and archived quotes. The output looks accurate to the agent, so a second agent uses the data to draft the proposal for the sales rep. No human checks either handoff. When it’s…

articles.headline: Trump makes final midterms pitch at Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool
articles.title: Trump makes final midterms pitch at Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool
articles.description: US President Donald Trump urged supporters to turn out ahead of Election Day

articles.headline: PM Modi credits renewable energy investments for softening West Asia crisis impact
articles.title: Clean energy investments helped India soften West Asia crisis impact: PM Modi
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi stated on November 2, 2026, that prior investments in renewable energy helped cushion India from the worst impacts of the West Asia crisis. Speaking at an expo in New Delhi, Modi projected $220 billion in investment opportunities for the sector by the end of the decade and highlighted the rapid expansion of domestic solar module manufacturing.
articles.description: Inaugurating Bharat Renewable Energy Summit & Expo, Narendra Modi says India’s economy continued to grow despite the crisis; warns that excess dependence on fossil fuels could risk increased exposure to global disruptions

articles.headline: Ebola outbreak death toll surpasses 5,300 across multiple nations
articles.title: Ebola outbreak kills more than 5,300 people in DR Congo
articles.summary: According to the Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention, the death toll from the ongoing Ebola outbreak has exceeded 5,300 fatalities. The Democratic Republic of the Congo remains the epicentre of the health crisis, with additional cases and deaths reported in Uganda, Kenya, Nigeria, and France involving the rare Bundibugyo strain of the virus.
articles.description: The Bundibugyo strain has spread to Kenya and Uganda, while two in Nigeria returned negative results.

articles.headline: Tasmac staff oppose new liquor bottle buyback scheme in Tamil Nadu
articles.title: Why are Tasmac staff opposing the liquor bottle ‘buyback’ scheme in Tamil Nadu? | Explained
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu State Marketing Corporation introduced a ten rupee environment cess and refund buyback scheme on November 1, 2026, prompting immediate protests and unplanned closures by outlet employees. Workers cited technical glitches in point-of-sale machines and inadequate storage space for returned bottles, following longstanding disputes over extra charges collected above the maximum retail price.
articles.description: Tasmac last week announced a ₹10 increase in the MRP of all liquor variants from November 1, 2026, by introducing an environment cess, with consumers eligible for a ₹10 refund upon returning empty bottles

articles.headline: Israeli electoral commission rejects Benjamin Netanyahu fraud allegations
articles.title: Israel election commission rejects Benjamin Netanyahu charges of fraud
articles.summary: Israeli electoral authorities rejected fraud allegations promoted by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu regarding Arab parties after auditing 9069 polling stations on November 4, 2026. President Isaac Herzog will receive the election results to decide who forms a government, as neither Netanyahu nor rival Gadi Eisenkot secured a majority in parliament. Netanyahu faces corruption charges, while the opposition urges unity to remove him.
articles.description: The Central Elections Committee said it had conducted an audit of 9,069 polling stations following complaints and was confident that the announced results accurately reflect the will of the voters

articles.headline: Uk Supreme Court hears appeal against Palestine Action proscription
articles.title: UK Supreme Court hears appeal against Palestine Action’s proscription
articles.summary: The United Kingdom Supreme Court in London has begun a two-day hearing challenging the government designation of Palestine Action as a terrorist organization. Huda Ammori, cofounder of the direct action group, argues the ban disproportionately restricts freedom of speech. Concurrently, police arrested approximately 25 demonstrators outside the court. Rights organizations, including Amnesty International, have condemned the proscription and criticized the misuse of terrorism legislation.
articles.description: Rights activists say UK decision against Palestine Action is a 'misuse of terrorism powers'.

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu launches battery energy storage systems policy to boost grid stability
articles.title: Tamil Nadu government releases three-year BESS policy
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government published a three-year storage policy on November 4, 2026, aiming to deploy 2.5 gigawatts of battery capacity. The Tamil Nadu Power Distribution Corporation will procure this capacity in the first phase. The framework mandates installations for new solar projects starting April 1, 2027, and offers transmission charge waivers to support the state's twenty-nine gigawatts of renewable energy.
articles.description: The policy aims to deploy 2.5 GW/10 GWh of Battery Energy Storage System during this period. The TNPDC will procure BESS capacity aggregating to 2,500 MW/10,000 MWh from eligible BESS projects

articles.headline: Bombay High Court advises Maharashtra to consider regulated firecracker timings
articles.title: Consider regulated timings for firecrackers, Bombay High Court tells Maharashtra government
articles.summary: The Bombay High Court suggested that the Maharashtra government and local authorities evaluate Supreme Court directives restricting Deepavali firecracker timings to curb severe pollution hazards. In a 13-page order issued on November 4, 2026, Justices Girish Kulkarni and Neela Gokhale also criticized the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation for selectively removing an awareness video featuring actress Dia Mirza following political objections.
articles.description: The Supreme Court had directed that the bursting of approved green crackers during Deepavali be restricted to specific windows between 6 a.m. and 7 a.m. and 8 p.m. to 10 p.m. in the NCR

articles.headline: Tenerife forward Jesus de Miguel dies after on-field collision
articles.title: Tenerife’s Jesus de Miguel remembered in moving tributes by football world
articles.summary: Jesus de Miguel, a 30-year-old forward for Spanish football club Tenerife, died on Tuesday following a fatal on-field collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a second division match. The player suffered a cardiac arrest after being transferred to an ambulance. In response to the tragedy, the Royal Spanish Football Federation suspended domestic matches until Friday, November 6, while European football governing body UEFA announced a minute of silence for all Champions League matches.
articles.description: The 30-year-old died on Tuesday following an on-pitch collision with Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono.

articles.headline: Sharp metal objects found in Halloween sweets across three European countries
articles.title: Sharp objects found in Halloween sweets in three European nations
articles.summary: Police issued warnings after needles, pins, screws, and nails were discovered inside Halloween sweets distributed to children in Germany, Austria, and Hungary. Authorities reported multiple injuries, including a nine-year-old girl in Germany and a ten-year-old girl in Austria. Austrian Interior Minister Gerhard Karner condemned the incidents as life-threatening, while German officials noted a significant increase in such reports compared to previous years.
articles.description: Dozens of cases are reported in Austria, Germany and Hungary, including a nine-year-old girl hurting her tongue while eating chocolate containing a pin.

articles.headline: Ravi Shankar Prasad says Punjab bears deep scars from riots and drugs
articles.title: Ravi Shankar Prasad says two blots stain Punjab’s soul: anti-Sikh riots, and drugs
articles.summary: Bharatiya Janata Party Lok Sabha Member of Parliament Ravi Shankar Prasad stated that the 1984 anti-Sikh riots and the drug crisis remain two major wounds on Punjab that require uncompromised justice. Speaking at a conclave in Punjab on November 4, 2026, the former union minister criticized the Congress party for previously shielding key leaders and attempting to politicize the sensitive issue through public events.
articles.description: The BJP MP and former Union Minister spoke at a day-long conclave titled ‘Zakhm 84 De’ (the wounds of 1984) organised by the Punjab BJP on the 1984 anti-Sikh riots

articles.headline: Can women work in Keralam’s toddy shops? Kerala High Court answers | Explained
articles.title: Can women work in Keralam’s toddy shops? Kerala High Court answers | Explained
articles.description: Can employers legally deny women jobs in certain industries in the name of workplace safety? Does the State have the right to restrict women’s employment to protect them from possible harassment?

articles.headline: Delhi authorities demolish settlements around historic mosque and relocate families
articles.title: 'We grew up around this historic Delhi mosque - now we have been forced out'
articles.summary: Authorities in Delhi demolished hundreds of homes across three settlements on October 7, relocating 717 families to Savda Ghevra on the city outskirts due to security concerns and illegal land usage. While the centuries-old mosque remains standing without water and electricity, the Delhi High Court scheduled a hearing for December 16 to address ongoing legal petitions regarding access and preservation.
articles.description: Authorities have razed hundreds of houses in a neighbourhood in central Delhi, saying they were built on government land.

articles.headline: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed becomes first Muslim US Senator-elect in Michigan
articles.title: Who is Abdul El-Sayed, first Muslim U.S. Senator-elect?
articles.summary: Democrat Abdul El-Sayed won Michigan's open Senate seat on Tuesday by defeating former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers. The 42-year-old former public health official secured a crucial victory that prevented Republicans from claiming the seat vacated by retiring Senator Gary Peters. El-Sayed campaigned on lowering living costs and reducing corporate influence, while overcoming unsupported Republican allegations regarding ties to the Muslim Brotherhood.
articles.description: Abdul El-Sayed is set to become the first Muslim to enter the U.S. Senate with his victory over former Republican lawmaker Mike Rogers in midterm elections

articles.headline: Karnataka government increases bus fares across four state-run transport corporations
articles.title: Karnataka hikes bus fares in BMTC, KSRTC, NWKRTC, and KKRTC
articles.summary: The Karnataka government revised bus fares upward by 23 percent to 35 percent across four state transport corporations, effective midnight on November 4, 2026. Transport Minister Byrathi Suresh stated that the adjustments, which affect ordinary, express, and airport services, were necessary due to rising diesel expenses and operational losses, falling below recommendations from the Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee.
articles.description: The fare revision is lower than the 45% increase recommended by the Public Transport Fare Regulatory Committee

articles.headline: Burglars steal 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal from hockey star M.M. Somaya
articles.title: 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal stolen from home of hockey star M.M. Somaya in Bengaluru
articles.summary: Unidentified burglars stole the 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal, international sporting medals, jewellery, and cash from the Bengaluru residence of former Indian hockey captain M.M. Somaya. The theft occurred in the early hours of October 28 while the family was away in Kodagu. Indiranagar police registered a case under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, and formed special teams to recover the irreplaceable national sporting honours.
articles.description: The incident, which took place in the early hours of October 28, came to light after the family returned from Kodagu district.

articles.headline: Elon Musk jokes about Republican losses following major campaign spending
articles.title: Musk makes light of defeats after record spend on Republican candidates
articles.summary: Democratic candidates secured control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives during the Tuesday elections, defeating the Republican Party across several traditional strongholds including Texas and Kansas. Technology executive Elon Musk reportedly contributed $446m to support Republican campaigns, primarily through America PAC and the Senate Leadership Fund. Following the defeats, Musk posted remarks on the social media platform X, suggesting alternative plans for artificial intelligence data centres. Democratic victor James Talarico and other successful candidates directly referenced Musk during their campaigns and victory speeches.
articles.description: Tesla and SpaceX founder Elon Musk is the world's richest man and the largest individual donor in the US midterms.

articles.headline: Small jet crashes in Florida neighbourhood, killing all nine people on board
articles.title: Plane may have broken apart ahead of deadly Florida jet crash, say investigators
articles.summary: A business jet traveling from Austin to the Bahamas crashed in Palm Beach County, Florida, killing all nine people on board. The Learjet 60 plummeted into a residential street on Sunday at approximately 12:50 EST, causing a massive explosion and damaging local infrastructure. According to the United States transport secretary, the Federal Aviation Administration is assisting a National Transportation Safety Board investigation into the tragedy.
articles.description: The National Transportation Safety Board also believes weather could have been a factor in the crash, but warns it is too early to determine the cause.

articles.headline: Sundaram Finance reports twenty-one percent profit increase in second quarter
articles.title: Sundaram Finance’s Q2 PAT up 21% to ₹475 cr.; disbursements grow 28%
articles.summary: Sundaram Finance reported a twenty-one percent year-on-year increase in standalone profit after tax to four hundred seventy-five crore rupees for the second quarter of financial year twenty-seven. Chennai-based non-banking financial company disbursements rose twenty-eight percent to ten thousand three hundred fifty-five crore rupees, supported by strong domestic economic momentum, improved asset quality, and expanding assets under management.
articles.description: Chennai-based NBFC reports 19% growth in assets under management to ₹65,992 crore; net Stage 3 assets improve to 0.91% as of September-end

articles.headline: European nations rehearse potential military deployment to Ukraine
articles.title: Thousands of European troops to rehearse Ukraine deployment in event of peace
articles.summary: Britain and France are leading a multinational military exercise in Poland involving nearly 3,000 personnel from 12 European nations. The training aims to test deployment capabilities for a potential reassurance force in Ukraine once peace is achieved, though Western officials stress the troops will not engage in offensive operations or act under NATO command.
articles.description: Western officials stress that any force sent to Ukraine would not take part in any offensive operations.

articles.headline: Canva restructures its workforce amidst the rapid growth of generative AI
articles.title: As Canva restructures, how is AI reshaping creative businesses? | Explained
articles.summary: Design platform Canva announced plans to reorganise its staff due to slowing growth and technological shifts. The company is navigating changes as generative AI reshapes creative businesses by altering how visual content is produced and sold. Other firms in the creative industry are similarly addressing the opportunities and challenges introduced by artificial intelligence across global markets.
articles.description: Canva says 1,271 jobs are affected by its reorganisation amid slowing growth. Adobe, Figma and Getty Images show how generative AI is reshaping products, costs and business models in the creative industry

articles.headline: Kerala draft report proposes higher minimum wages and bonus eligibility
articles.title: Draft report on implementation of Labour Codes moots higher minimum wages, wider eligibility for bonus
articles.summary: A newly submitted draft report on implementing four Labour Codes recommends expanding worker family units and increasing minimum wage calculations. Submitted to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on November 4, 2026, the panel also proposes mandatory free medical check-ups for hazardous occupations and enhanced safety provisions for female night-shift workers across the state.
articles.description: The draft report was submitted by Minister for Labour Bindhu Krishna to Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan on Wednesday.

articles.title: Can women work in Keralam’s toddy shops? Kerala High Court answers | Explained
articles.description: Can employers legally deny women jobs in certain industries in the name of workplace safety? Does the State have the right to restrict women’s employment to protect them from possible harassment?

articles.headline: Thailand requires formal Chinese extradition request for detained Uyghur men
articles.title: China must make extradition request if it wants two Uyghur men returned: Thailand
articles.summary: National Security Council head Chaipruak Doungprapat stated that China must file a formal extradition request to deport two detained Uyghur men. While human rights advocates express fears of torture if returned, the judicial process will determine their fate following letters pleading against deportation from the Suan Plu immigration detention centre in Bangkok.
articles.description: The two men, in letters shared last week, pleaded not to be sent back to China

articles.headline: Milky Way grew by consuming nearby galaxies and leaving stellar streams
articles.title: The Milky Way grew by devouring galaxies, leaving a trail of ghost stars
articles.summary: Galactic archaeologists studying stellar ages, chemical compositions, and motions discovered that the Milky Way expanded over nearly 12 billion years by devouring smaller galaxies like the Magellanic clouds. These violent collisions rip apart smaller galaxies, leaving behind distinct stellar streams that reveal the evolutionary history of our galaxy.
articles.description: Galactic archaeologists are using precise measures and larger sample sizes afforded by new missions to tease apart minute differences between groups of stars, revealing the history of the Milky Way going back almost 12 billion years

articles.headline: Supreme Court stays Madras High Court order on Chidambaram temple administration
articles.title: SC stays Madras HC order on Chidambaram temple
articles.summary: The Supreme Court froze a Madras High Court order that formed a Board of Management to administer the ancient Chidambaram Sabanayagar Temple in Tamil Nadu. Justices Aravind Kumar and Vipul M. Pancholi questioned state high court jurisdiction over public temples during the November 4, 2026 hearing after challenges from the Podhu Dikshidar hereditary priests.
articles.description: Questions whether High Courts have parens patriae jurisdiction only over public temples and not places of worship of other faiths

articles.headline: India records below average monsoon despite shaping El Nino
articles.title: Why even a strong El Niño does not guarantee a poor Indian monsoon
articles.summary: The 2026 southwest monsoon concluded nearly thirteen percent below the long term average of eighty seven centimeters, accompanied by a developing El Nino expected to peak in December. East and Northeast India experienced their driest season since records began in 1901. Historically, strong El Nino events do not always guarantee poor monsoon outcomes.
articles.description: Seven Indian monsoons since 1950 have run into a moderate or strong El Niño. Of these, in five years, including 2026, monsoon rainfall levels were at least 10% lower than the long-term average. The IMD refers to this level as 'deficient’. The 2023 season was something of an exception with ‘below average’ rainfall. However, 1997 had ‘average’ rainfall

articles.headline: Asaduddin Owaisi criticises electoral revision process after no illegal immigrants found
articles.title: With no illegal immigrants found on draft electoral rolls, SIR greatly inconvenienced people: Owaisi
articles.summary: Hyderabad parliamentarian Asaduddin Owaisi stated that the Special Intensive Revision process caused unnecessary hardship for poor daily wage earners despite election officials finding zero foreign nationals on the draft rolls. Speaking on November 4, 2026, the AIMIM president also condemned federal efforts to remove the historic Qadeemic Masjid inside New Delhi's Krishi Bhavan complex.
articles.description: Qadeemi Masjid was there before Delhi became the national capital, says AIMIM president

articles.headline: South Africa holds local elections amid declining support for African National Congress
articles.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
articles.summary: South Africans voted in local elections on November 4, 2026, with polls indicating a substantial decline in support for the ruling African National Congress due to widespread public frustration over unemployment, crime, and deteriorating basic service delivery across municipalities. The African National Congress previously lost its parliamentary majority. Analysts predict the party will record its worst electoral performance as competing political entities vie to govern nearly 300 municipal regions.
articles.description: As South Africans vote in local elections, residents tell the BBC they are tired of the poor quality of services they get.

articles.headline: NBA confirms removal of Rwandan army team over US sanctions
articles.title: Rwanda's army team removed from Africa league after US sanctions, NBA says
articles.summary: The National Basketball Association confirmed it removed Rwanda's army-funded Armée Patriotique Rwandaise club from the Basketball Africa League due to United States sanctions imposed in March. Responding to a congressional inquiry on October 23, 2026, league officials stated the team will remain barred while sanctions against Rwanda's military and defense ministry for activities in the Democratic Republic of Congo stay in place.
articles.description: The US imposed sanctions on Rwanda's army over its role in the conflict in DR Congo.

articles.headline: Union Cabinet approves 14,500 crore rupees funding scheme for energy storage systems
articles.title: Cabinet clears ₹14,500 crore viability gap funding scheme for 92 GWh battery energy storage systems
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet approved fourteen thousand five hundred crore rupees in viability gap funding on Wednesday for grid-scale energy storage systems spanning financial year 2027 through financial year 2031. Information and Broadcasting Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw stated in New Delhi that the initiative supports ninety-two gigawatt-hours of storage capacity across three technologies to help India achieve its target of five hundred gigawatts of renewable energy by 2030.
articles.description: The scheme is aimed at supporting the development of 92 GWh storage capacity across three technologies — Battery Energy Storage System (30 GWh), Pumped Storage Projects (60 GWh) and Emerging Storage Technologies (2GW)

articles.headline: Modi and Naidu review cyclone devastation in Andhra Pradesh
articles.title: Modi calls Naidu, reviews damage from Cyclones Arnab and Murasu
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke with Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu on November 4, 2026, to review recovery efforts following Cyclones Arnab and Murasu. Naidu reported severe damage to agriculture, roads, and power infrastructure, requesting ₹4,563 crore in immediate aid for Cyclone Arnab alone, while preliminary assessments place Cyclone Murasu damages at ₹343 crore according to the Chief Minister’s Office.
articles.description: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister seeks Central assistance for losses suffered by farmers and damage to roads and power lines

articles.headline: Asia-Pacific nations watch United States midterms amid economic strain
articles.title: War, tariffs and China: What the US midterms mean for the Asia-Pacific
articles.summary: Governments and businesses across the Asia-Pacific region are closely monitoring United States midterm elections following severe energy shortages and tariffs. Analysts note that while regional leaders hope for significant policy shifts regarding trade and the war on Iran, a divided United States Congress is unlikely to alter presidential decisions.
articles.description: Hit hard by Trump's tariffs and the war on Iran, countries in the Asia-Pacific want 'enormous changes' in US policies.

articles.headline: P.V. Sindhu discusses rebuilding career after winning Hylo Open
articles.title: With two titles in 4 months, P.V. Sindhu says she is building, not chasing her old self
articles.summary: Indian badminton player P.V. Sindhu secured her second title in four months at the Hylo Open on November 1, 2026, returning to world number six. The thirty-one-year-old attributed her resurgence to a revamped support team, including her husband. She emphasised proper rest, recovery, and preparation for the upcoming fifteen-point scoring format changes while praising emerging female players.
articles.description: The switch to a 15-point scoring format from next year will demand another adjustment, and Sindhu believes players will have less time to recover from a slow start

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate raids former APPSC secretary over recruitment irregularities
articles.title: ED searches IPS officer Sitarama Anjaneyulu, others in APPSC Group-I evaluation case
articles.summary: Enforcement Directorate officials conducted searches across seven locations in Hyderabad, Secunderabad, and Guntur district on November 4, 2026. The raids targeted former Andhra Pradesh Public Service Commission secretary P. Sitarama Anjaneyulu and CamSign Media owner P. Madhusudhan Rao regarding alleged manual evaluation irregularities in the 2020 Group-I recruitment examination following a Prevention of Money Laundering Act case registration.
articles.description: ED officials search the houses of retired IPS officer P. Sitarama Anjaneyulu and CamSign Media owner P. Madhusudhan Rao and the Haailand resort in Guntur district

articles.headline: Indian-origin candidates contest across United States midterm elections
