articles.title: Who are the Indian-origin candidates in U.S. midterm elections?
articles.summary: Numerous individuals with South Asian heritage are running for public office in the November 2026 legislative contests across various American states. Prominent incumbent lawmakers and new nominees are seeking positions in Congress, state executive offices, and local governments. These campaigns encompass multiple jurisdictions, highlighting the growing political participation of this community within the American electoral system.
articles.description: Democratic lawmakers Ro Khanna, Pramila Jayapal, Ami Bera and Suhas Subramanyam are seeking re-election to the U.S. Congress

articles.headline: Indian sailor killed in suspected drone attack off Oman coast
articles.title: Attack on vessel near Hormuz Strait: Deceased sailor hailed from Gujarat, kin plan burial in Oman
articles.summary: A twenty-five-year-old sailor from Gujarat named Nahim Ajij Gandhar died following a suspected drone attack on an Indian-flagged cargo vessel near the Strait of Oman on November 2, 2026. Thirteen other crew members survived and were rescued by the Omani Coast Guard. The vessel and its date consignment were destroyed, prompting India to urge diplomatic solutions and safe passage corridors.
articles.description: Nahim Ajij Gandhar was among the 14 crew members on board the vessel, which was registered at Bedi port in Gujarat’s Jamnagar district

articles.headline: INCOIS issues marine heat wave and swell surge warnings for India
articles.title: INCOIS warns of Marine Heat Wave, issues swell surge alert for east and west coasts
articles.summary: The Indian National Centre for Ocean Information Services issued a marine heat wave warning across the Arabian Sea, Indian Ocean, and Bay of Bengal on November 4, 2026. Additionally, officials issued a swell surge warning for both the east and west coasts, including the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where waves exceeding one metre are expected to impact coastal ecosystems.
articles.description: The warming conditions could adversely affect coral reef ecosystems, marine productivity and coastal biodiversity

articles.headline: U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio meets Venezuelan counterpart in Washington
articles.title: Rubio meets Venezuelan counterpart as U.S. presses for progress on election preparations
articles.summary: United States Secretary of State Marco Rubio held discussions with Venezuelan Foreign Minister Oliver Blanco in Washington to advance preparations for upcoming elections. The diplomatic engagement follows a recent electoral reform blueprint agreed upon by local authorities and opposition figures, as the administration of President Donald Trump continues monitoring political developments after the ouster of former leader Nicolás Maduro.
articles.description: The meeting held on November 2 was one of the highest-level encounters between a senior Trump administration official and a counterpart from acting President Delcy Rodríguez's government

articles.headline: President Donald Trump faces low approval ratings ahead of midterm elections
articles.title: Trump approval rating near record low on eve of US midterm elections: Poll
articles.summary: United States President Donald Trump approaches the midterm elections with a job approval rating lingering near historical lows, according to recent polling data. While the president campaigned extensively to support Republican candidates trying to maintain congressional control, surveys indicate widespread voter dissatisfaction driven by economic concerns and inflation following regional conflicts.
articles.description: Only 32 percent of voters approve of Trump's job performance in the latest Reuters/Ipsos poll.

articles.headline: Can Russia compete with the US, China and the EU in Africa?
articles.title: Can Russia compete with the US, China and the EU in Africa?
articles.description: Moscow pledges more trade and investment in Africa, where leaders want local industries, technology and jobs.

articles.headline: India opts to bowl first in opening ODI against New Zealand
articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st ODI: Pacers, Kohli script impressive win for India
articles.summary: India captain Shubman Gill elected to field first against New Zealand in the opening One Day International in Auckland on November 4, 2026. The visiting team deployed four specialist fast bowlers alongside spin-bowling all-rounder Naman Dhir. New Zealand captain Mitchell Santner leads the hosts in the match, which features a confirmed lineup including veteran batsmen Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma.
articles.description: India reached the revised target of 143 in 22.4 overs of the rain-curtalied match with Kohli’s 51-ball knock doing bulk of the damage

articles.headline: Ugandan critics face abductions and legal charges over online posts
articles.title: ‘I will not delete my posts’: Inside Uganda’s crackdown on online critics
articles.summary: Ugandan authorities have detained citizens and critics, including Praise Aloikin Opoloje and journalist Andrew Tabandama Natumanya, over social media posts and reporting criticizing powerful figures such as President Yoweri Museveni and military chief General Muhoozi Kainerugaba. Victims allege they were abducted by armed men in Toyota HiAce vans, assaulted, and threatened before facing formal court charges or brief detentions. The crackdown highlights ongoing risks for individuals using digital platforms to challenge the government in Kampala.
articles.description: Uganda’s online critics allege abductions and intimidation as families search for missing relatives.

articles.headline: South Korean appeals court upholds former President Yoon Suk Yeol conviction
articles.title: Seoul court upholds ex-President Yoon’s election conviction
articles.summary: A South Korean appeals court on Wednesday upheld former President Yoon Suk Yeol’s 18-month suspended sentence for spreading disinformation during his campaign. The ruling affirms a lower court verdict regarding false statements about his ties to a shaman. If the Supreme Court upholds the decision, Yoon's 2022 election victory could be invalidated and his former party, the People Power Party, would be forced to repay nearly thirty million dollars in campaign expenses.
articles.description: The ruling affirmed a lower court verdict that found Mr. Yoon guilty of violating election laws by making false statements during his campaign, including lying about his ties to a shaman

articles.headline: Who holds the power today? Governments or corporations?
articles.title: Who holds the power today? Governments or corporations?
articles.description: Who holds the power today? Governments or corporations?

articles.headline: Voters prioritize economy and cost of living ahead of U.S. midterms
articles.title: US midterms 2026: What polls reveal about Democratic, Republican voters
articles.summary: Voters across the United States head to the polls as surveys highlight deep divisions over economic conditions, personal finances, and key policy issues between Democrats and Republicans. While economic concerns remain paramount for both parties, voters diverge significantly regarding the importance of healthcare, immigration, and trust in leadership during the current congressional midterm elections.
articles.description: From the economy and cost of living to immigration, polls suggest where American voters agree and disagree.

articles.headline: Transport corporation employees protest after injured Telangana bus conductor dies.
articles.title: Telangana bus conductor Pravalika, who was pushed off moving bus, dies; she took up RTC job after father’s death
articles.summary: Telangana State Road Transport Corporation employees staged widespread demonstrations across Khammam after twenty-four-year-old conductor G. Pravalika succumbed to injuries sustained on October 25. The employee had been allegedly pushed from a moving bus by a passenger during a ticket dispute. Police altered the charges against the arrested suspect following the worker's death, prompting transport workers to demand stricter safety measures.
articles.description: Her death sparks outrage. TGSRTC staff protest across Khammam region.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh water resources minister puts officials on alert for cyclone rainfall.
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu: Ramanaidu puts irrigation officials on high alert over swollen rivers, drains
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Water Resources Minister Nimmala Ramanaidu ordered irrigation officials to maintain high vigilance on Wednesday due to heavy downpours from Cyclone Murasu. The minister instructed authorities to drain stagnant agricultural water, monitor rising river levels, and manage flood flows across multiple districts. Officials were further directed to ensure coordinated emergency responses to protect crops and public safety.
articles.description: The Nallamada and Parchur drains are flowing above their maximum levels around Parchur, Bapatla and Chirala

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh chief minister urges central assistance for stranded chilli consignments
articles.title: Naidu writes to Piyush Goyal on 150 chilli containers held at Colombo port over moisture content
articles.summary: Andhra Pradesh Chief Minister N. Chandrababu Naidu wrote to Union Commerce and Industry Minister Piyush Goyal on November 4, 2026, seeking help to export over 150 chilli containers stranded at the Colombo port in Sri Lanka. Valued at sixty crore rupees, the shipments intended for Asian markets were held due to high moisture content, prompting concerns over farmer losses.
articles.description: Seeks immediate assistance for losses caused by cyclones Arnab and Murasu; raises issue of chilli consignments stranded at Colombo port

articles.headline: Karnataka electoral rolls reveal hundreds of linked voter IDs after revision
articles.title: In Karnataka seat where ‘vote chori’ claims first surfaced, over 800 voter IDs linked to 397 names after SIR
articles.summary: An analysis by The Hindu following a special intensive revision revealed that Mahadevapura constituency in Karnataka has over eight hundred voter IDs linked to less than four hundred individuals. The seat previously faced vote manipulation allegations. According to the Chief Electoral Officer, no formal complaints have been received, though social media reports will be verified.
articles.description: In the Mahadevapura Assembly constituency, some voters were found listed in the final rolls with the same EPIC number in two different constituencies; in some other cases, voters were issued multiple EPIC IDs

articles.headline: Palestinian flag appears widely in European protests and demonstrations
articles.title: From education to housing protests, Palestine’s flag spreads across Europe
articles.summary: Palestinian flags and keffiyehs have increasingly appeared at demonstrations across Europe concerning education, housing, and the cost of living. While activists view the symbols as a broader nod against anti-colonialism and global inequality, critics and some Palestinians argue that incorporating the flag risks diluting its original meaning and conflating distinct local struggles with the ongoing conflict in the Middle East.
articles.description: Symbols such as the flag and keffiyeh represent anti-colonial struggles but some question their use amid mass rallies.

articles.headline: Indonesian presidential chief of staff dismissed over illegal wiretapping allegations
articles.title: Indonesian president’s chief of staff dismissed over alleged wiretapping
articles.summary: Indonesian President Prabowo Subianto dismissed chief of staff Listyo Sigit Prabowo on November 4, 2026, following his arrest alongside two senior police officers for alleged illegal wiretapping. Presidential spokesperson Prasetyo Hadi stated the unauthorized surveillance targeting high-profile figures could constitute treason and endanger state safety, while the military deployed over 20,000 soldiers in Jakarta as a security measure.
articles.description: Gov't says Listyo may have committed 'treason' after he is arrested and accused of wiretapping top officials' phones.

articles.headline: Union Cabinet considers capital support schemes for critical minerals and storage
articles.title: Union Cabinet to discuss capex support for critical mineral processing, VGF for RE grid-scale storage system
articles.summary: The Union Cabinet scheduled a meeting on November 4, 2026, to review two major policy initiatives proposed in an official memo. The measures involve capital expenditure support for critical mineral processing plants to secure supply chains and viability gap funding to develop grid-scale renewable energy storage systems across transmission networks.
articles.description: The Hindu had learnt previously that the potential scheme could provide support of about 30% for setting up of these processing plants

articles.headline: Democrats take control of United States Senate and House in midterm elections
articles.title: How America voted in maps and charts
articles.summary: The Democratic Party secured control of both the United States Senate and the House of Representatives during the midterm elections, according to projections by CBS News on November 4, 2026. Democrats achieved significant victories in states including South Carolina, Texas, and Iowa. Exit polling indicated that voters viewed the economy as the primary concern, with a majority expressing dissatisfaction with Donald Trump's economic policies.
articles.description: See the maps and charts that show how America voted in the US midterm elections.

articles.headline: Survey shows Syrians view Israel as primary regional security threat
articles.title: Syrians see Israel as biggest regional threat, followed by Iran: Survey
articles.summary: According to a nationwide survey published in 2026 by the Doha-based Arab Center for Research and Policy Studies and the Arab Center for Contemporary Syria Studies, sixty-one percent of Syrian respondents named Israel as their country's main threat, while twenty percent cited Iran. The Arab Opinion Index revealed widespread opposition to recognizing Israel and ongoing public division regarding direct diplomatic talks between Syrian and Israeli officials.
articles.description: Some 97% of respondents to Arab Opinion Index for Syria say Israel threatens security and stability in the Middle East.

articles.headline: Essar Renewables signs power purchase agreement with NHPC for 300 megawatt project
articles.title: Essar Renewables signs Power Purchase Agreement with NHPC for 300 MW project
articles.summary: Essar Power signed a power purchase agreement with NHPC for a three hundred megawatt project integrating solar, wind, and battery storage systems. Essar will invest about four thousand five hundred crore rupees in the initiative. Chief Executive Officer Ankur Kumar stated the project marks a significant milestone in building a five gigawatt diversified energy portfolio across India.
articles.description: Essar Power will invest about ₹4,500 crore in the project, which will integrate solar, wind and Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS) to deliver and dispatchable renewable power

articles.headline: India and Bangladesh maintain engagement through Joint River Commission mechanism
articles.title: India-Bangladesh Joint River Commission | Explained
articles.summary: The Ministry of External Affairs confirmed that India and Bangladesh will continue collaborating through their Joint River Commission to address water-related issues, including the Ganga Water Treaty expiring on December twelve, 2026. Both nations share approximately fifty-four rivers, with three major waterways playing vital roles in agricultural and flood-management systems established following the war of 1971.
articles.description: Following the war of 1971, India and Bangladesh agreed to establish a Joint River Commission to deal with all river-water-related issues between the two sides

articles.headline: Democratic candidates lead multiple key races in California midterm elections
articles.title: Key takeaways from the 2026 midterm elections in California
articles.summary: Democratic candidates have pulled ahead in several crucial contests during California midterm elections marked by partisan redistricting and proposed tax measures. Former state Attorney General Xavier Becerra won the gubernatorial race against Republican Steve Hilton, while competitive congressional and ballot measure outcomes remained unresolved as votes continued to be tallied across the western state.
articles.description: Democrats easily hold on to governor's office and are on track to notch up wins in key congressional races.

articles.headline: Iran balances diplomatic negotiations with security establishment power dynamics
articles.title: Who determines Iran’s fighting and negotiating position amid US threats?
articles.summary: President Masoud Pezeshkian stated that his government received specific authorities from Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei regarding ongoing negotiations with the United States to prevent further military escalation. Following US and Israeli air strikes that killed former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, decision-making power has shifted toward security bodies including the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Supreme National Security Council.
articles.description: Iran is on the brink of a new escalation with the US, but negotiations are continuing.

articles.headline: Reserve Bank of India constitutes new technical committee for financial markets
articles.title: RBI constitutes Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets
articles.summary: The Reserve Bank of India announced the formation of the Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets to engage with stakeholders on operational matters regarding money and foreign exchange markets. Chaired by the Deputy Governor in charge of the Financial Markets Regulation Department, the committee includes seven external members and will convene at least once a quarter following announcements made by Governor Sanjay Malhotra.
articles.description: RBI sets up expert panel to advise on market structure, liquidity, and infrastructure amid evolving financial markets and policy shifts

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh deploys disaster response teams ahead of Cyclone Murasu
articles.title: Cyclonic storm Murasu to make landfall close to Ongole
articles.summary: Authorities in Andhra Pradesh have deployed six National Disaster Response Force teams and seven State Disaster Response Force teams across vulnerable districts as Cyclone Murasu approaches. According to the India Meteorological Department, the storm is expected to make landfall near Ongole with wind speeds up to 120 kilometers per hour in the early hours of November 3, 2026.
articles.description: NDRF, SDRF teams deployed in districts likely to be affected

articles.headline: US midterms campaign projected to reach nearly twelve billion dollars in spending
articles.title: Musk pumps $446m into US midterms, as campaign spending set to 'shatter' records
articles.summary: The United States midterm elections are on track to become the most expensive on record, with total spending projected to reach nearly twelve billion dollars according to the tracking organisation Open Secrets. Outside political groups and Super Political Action Committees have driven the majority of these expenditures. Billionaire Elon Musk emerged as the top individual donor, contributing almost half a billion dollars to support Republican candidates, particularly in Texas.
articles.description: The 2026 campaign is projected to cost nearly $12bn - BBC Verify looks into where all that money has come from.

articles.headline: United States to suspend South Africa and Rwanda from trade pact
articles.title: US to suspend South Africa and Rwanda from duty-free trade access
articles.summary: The United States announced it will remove South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act duty-free trade programme starting January 1, 2027. United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer stated that both nations failed to meet eligibility criteria regarding governance and trade barriers. South Africa exported about one point seven billion dollars in goods under the scheme in 2025.
articles.description: South Africa to lose duty-free access, affecting $1.7bn worth of annual exports, including cars and farm products.

articles.headline: Australian government defends social media ban for under 16s in court
articles.title: Australian government defends social media ban for under 16s in court
articles.summary: Government lawyers defended a law restricting social media for children under 16 before the country highest court during a hearing in Canberra. The measure is being challenged by Reddit and the Digital Freedom Project over freedom of expression concerns. Five million accounts have closed since December, though officials acknowledged younger users still bypass age verification processes.
articles.description: Government lawyers argued that social media use posed risks to children, and action is needed to protect them.

articles.headline: Israeli prime minister pushes for military strikes against Iran
articles.title: Netanyahu pressing Trump to attack Iran after midterms, says officials
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is urging United States President Donald Trump to launch air strikes against Iran following the November midterm elections. Regional officials report the push aims to help form an emergency government after coalition losses. Meanwhile, Qatari mediators are pursuing diplomatic talks to halt attacks in the Strait of Hormuz in exchange for lifting port blockades.
articles.description: A return to full-scale war with Iran could help Benjamin Netanyahu to form an emergency government after he and his far-right allies lost their parliamentary majority in last week's elections

articles.headline: Amit Shah defends voter list revisions during Hyderabad political event
articles.title: Amit Shah backs SIR, alleges 3 crore ‘illegal infiltrators’ identified in 13 crore deleted voters
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah claimed on November 2, 2026, that the Election Commission of India removed three crore illegal infiltrators from Bangladesh during the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. Speaking in Hyderabad, he criticized opposition leaders for opposing the exercise and challenged Rahul Gandhi to a parliamentary debate regarding voter list integrity.

articles.headline: Indian foreign secretary meets Nepal foreign minister to discuss bilateral ties
articles.title: Foreign Secretary Misri meets Nepal Foreign Minister, discusses bilateral ties
articles.summary: Indian Foreign Secretary Vikram Misri met Nepalese Foreign Minister Shisir Khanal in Kathmandu on November 4, 2026, to discuss cooperation in energy, trade, education, and sports. The official two-day visit aims to prepare for Prime Minister Balendra Shah proposed trip to New Delhi later in the month, according to statements from the Nepal Foreign Ministry.
articles.description: The diplomat is in Nepal on a two-day official visit aimed at preparing the ground for Nepalese Prime Minister Balendra Shah's proposed visit to New Delhi.

articles.headline: Green hydrogen production threatens water supplies and marine life
articles.title: North Africa’s green hydrogen exports to Europe could harm water supply and marine life: study
articles.summary: Generating green hydrogen through water electrolysis offers zero emissions for heavy industries like steel manufacturing and maritime shipping, but requires massive water consumption. According to a study published on November 4, 2026, African regions possessing the strongest solar and wind resources for this renewable energy source simultaneously suffer from the most severe water scarcity on earth.
articles.description: The research found that producing green hydrogen in desert areas in Australia, Chile and north Africa needs far more water than the industry claims. It also found serious environmental risks that had been overlooked

articles.headline: Tamil Nadu government sanctions funds for Bengal fox and jackal conservation
articles.title: Tamil Nadu takes baby steps towards conservation of Bengal fox, golden jackal
articles.summary: The Tamil Nadu government sanctioned one point three crore rupees this year to implement a conservation plan for Indian Bengal foxes and golden jackals. Both predators are protected under Schedule I of the Wildlife Protection Act of 1972. Surveys by the Advanced Institute for Wildlife Conservation showed their populations have dwindled over the past three to four decades.
articles.description: The State government has sanctioned ₹1.3 crore this year for comprehensive assessment of current threats, habitat use, and distribution patterns to develop an effective, long-term conservation roadmap.

articles.headline: Andhra Pradesh faces heavy rainfall as cyclone Murasu weakens into depression
articles.title: Murasu weakens into depression; heavy rain continues in coastal Andhra Pradesh
articles.summary: Persistent heavy rainfall affected coastal Andhra Pradesh on November 4, 2026, following the gradual weakening of cyclonic storm Murasu into a depression. According to the India Meteorological Department and the Directorate of Economics and Statistics, districts such as Palnadu and Kakinada recorded extreme rainfall measurements exceeding 250 millimetres, prompting widespread downpours across the central coastal belt.
articles.description: Edlapadu in Palnadu district records 269.45 mm in 24 hours, the highest in the State

articles.headline: Delhi air quality deteriorates to very poor category ahead of Diwali celebrations
articles.title: Delhi air quality worsens ahead of Diwali as firework restrictions enter force
articles.summary: Delhi implemented emergency anti-pollution measures under the Graded Response Action Plan as air quality index levels surpassed 300 ahead of Diwali. Authorities cited falling temperatures, slow wind speeds, and agricultural stubble burning in neighbouring regions as primary drivers for the hazardous smog, while the Supreme Court permitted restricted use of certified green firecrackers during specific holiday hours.
articles.description: On Wednesday morning, Delhi's air quality index reading stood at 377, in the "very poor" category.

articles.headline: Gianni Infantino is ineligible for re-election under FIFA statutes, says Maduro
articles.title: FIFA’s Infantino ineligible for re-election, says former governance chief
articles.summary: Miguel Maduro, the former head of FIFA's governance committee, stated that football body president Gianni Infantino cannot legally seek a fourth term in March 2027. Citing article 33 of FIFA statutes, Maduro argued that three-term limits apply regardless of incomplete mandates, while human rights groups separately urged member associations to challenge the candidacy ahead of upcoming deadlines.
articles.description: Miguel ⁠⁠Maduro insists Gianni Infantino cannot serve more than three terms, pointing to FIFA's statutes.

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate raids locations in Keralam and Tamil Nadu over coop society
articles.title: ED raids 11 locations in Keralam, Tamil Nadu over alleged money laundering linked to BLM cooperative society
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate conducted searches at eleven locations in Keralam and Tamil Nadu on November 4, 2026, targeting individuals linked to the Bharath Lajhna Multi State Co-operative Society. According to agency sources, the raids stemmed from an investigation into founding member R. Premkumar for alleged money laundering and public fund misappropriation. The society operates around 150 branches with over 15 lakh members.
articles.description: Searches at locations in cities, including Kochi, Kozhikode and Chennai, linked to R. Premkumar, founding member and de facto chairman and managing director of BLM, and some others

articles.headline: Hyderabad police arrest two men following viral video of women being slapped
articles.title: Two held after video of women being slapped over allegations of religious conversion goes viral
articles.summary: Meerpet police arrested two men named Lakshmi Narayana and Sashivardhan in Hyderabad on November 3, 2026, after a video surfaced showing two Christian women being slapped and verbally abused. The victims were attacked in Almasguda over unverified allegations of religious conversion, prompting condemnation from local politicians who emphasised that disputes must be handled through lawful channels.
articles.description: Meerpet Police in Hyderabad book a case after video of women being slapped and threatened over alleged religious conversions goes viral

articles.headline: Keralam government defends power purchase decision citing financial savings
articles.title: Power purchase row: Keralam govt opted for GNA offer over Himachal Pradesh deal to avoid ₹2,200 crore extra liability, says CM
articles.summary: Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan stated on November 4, 2026, that his administration chose power supply from GNA Energy OTC over an offer from the Himachal Pradesh government to prevent an additional financial burden exceeding ₹2,200 crore. Addressing a press briefing, the Chief Minister dismissed Opposition allegations linking the procurement to the transfer of Kerala State Electricity Board chairman M.G. Rajamanickam.
articles.description: Satheesan refutes Opposition charge that transfer of M.G. Rajamanickam as chairman and managing director of KSEB was linked to the power purchases

articles.headline: Odisha village landslide rescue operation suspended due to bad weather
articles.title: Rescue operation at landslide-hit south Odisha village halted; families prepare for final rituals
articles.summary: Multi-agency rescue operations at Gidipabali village in south Odisha were suspended on November 4, 2026, due to adverse weather conditions and nearly 30 feet of debris. Kandhamal District Collector Vedbhusan stated that families of 10 missing persons prepared for final rituals after multiple agencies failed to achieve breakthroughs following the October 30 landslide triggered by Cyclone Arnab.
articles.description: The decision to temporarily suspend the operation was taken after experts assessed that the remains, if any, could be buried under nearly 30 feet of debris, Kandhamal District Collector Vedbhusan said

articles.headline: Enforcement Directorate raids locations in Odisha and West Bengal over investment fraud
articles.title: ED raids in Odisha, Bengal in investment 'fraud' case'
articles.summary: The Enforcement Directorate conducted searches across ten premises in Odisha and West Bengal on November 4, 2026, as part of a money laundering investigation involving ₹120 crore. Based on an Odisha Police Economic Offences Wing First Information Report, the probe targets Kalpana Financial Services and director Amit Mandal for allegedly inducing depositors with false promises of fixed monthly returns.
articles.description: The promoters of the scheme collected about ₹120 crore from the public, according to the ED

articles.headline: Israel's President Herzog begins consultations to form new coalition government
articles.title: Israel's unassuming President Herzog holds keys to next government
articles.summary: President Isaac Herzog initiated party consultations on November 4, 2026, to select a candidate capable of forming a new coalition government. Neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu nor rival Gadi Eisenkot secured a parliamentary majority in the October 27 vote. Operating with broad legal discretion, the 66-year-old president aims to prevent a new election while managing domestic and international pressures.
articles.description: Isaac Herzog said he would do everything he could to avoid a fresh election — a possibility if neither camp can cobble together a coalition — including backing a unity government between Netanyahu and Eisenkot

articles.headline: US House Speaker Johnson rants about Marxism after Democrat gains
articles.title: US House Speaker Johnson rants about Marxism after Democrat gains
articles.description: US House Speaker Johnson rants about Marxism after Democrat gains

articles.headline: United States administration petitions Supreme Court to block California ballots
articles.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump request to set aside California ballots
articles.summary: The administration of United States President Donald Trump filed an emergency request with the Supreme Court to halt California from counting mail-in ballots from over twenty thousand alleged non-citizens. The Department of Justice argues these votes must be isolated until citizenship is verified, while California officials contend the list is unreliable and disenfranchises legitimate voters. Lower federal courts previously rejected the administration requests.
articles.description: Top court declines to block California from counting ballots of voters Trump administration claims are not US citizens.

articles.headline: Underrepresented candidates achieve historic milestones in United States midterm elections
articles.title: Firsts for women and minorities in US midterm elections
articles.summary: Voters across several United States regions elected candidates from diverse backgrounds to major legislative and gubernatorial positions during the midterm elections. Historic wins included the country's first openly gay senator Chris Pappas in New Hampshire, first Muslim senator Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, and multiple female governors and minority officials taking office nationwide.
articles.description: The elections, which saw Democrats make big gains, also marked firsts for women and minorities in major offices.

articles.headline: Keralam chief minister criticises former governor over public service commission recommendation
articles.title: Keralam CM flays ex-Governor Arlekar over recommendation to remove PSC chief; justifies IAS reshuffle
articles.summary: Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan criticised former Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar on Wednesday for recommending the removal of Kerala Public Service Commission chairman M.R. Baiju without proper consultation. Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram, Satheesan justified recent administrative IAS transfers and announced that the state government will soon unveil a new liquor policy following controversies over bar licenses.
articles.description: Satheesan says former Governor’s recommendation was made without following due procedure and that the latter should have consulted the State government before making such a move with the President

articles.headline: Kotak Mahindra Bank receives regulatory approval to acquire Deutsche Bank India assets
articles.title: Kotak Mahindra Bank gets CCI nod to acquire Deutsche Bank India's retail, private banking businesses
articles.summary: Kotak Mahindra Bank has obtained approval from the Competition Commission of India on November 4, 2026, to acquire the retail banking, private banking, and wealth management operations of Deutsche Bank in the country. The transaction involves customer-facing businesses and portfolios including loans and deposits, allowing the domestic financial services conglomerate to further expand its presence.
articles.description: The transaction will be undertaken as a going concern on a slump sale basis by Kotak Mahindra Bank from the seller, the CCI said

articles.headline: Kotak Mahindra Bank agrees to acquire Deutsche Bank India retail business
articles.title: Why Deutsche Bank is exiting its retail business in India | Explained
articles.summary: Kotak Mahindra Bank agreed to acquire Deutsche Bank India's retail banking, affluent private banking, and wealth management operations for 281 crore rupees on July 1, 2026. The transaction strengthens the domestic lender's market position while enabling Deutsche Bank to concentrate entirely on its core corporate and institutional banking services for approximately 1,50,000 customers.
articles.description: Why is Deutsche Bank exiting? Why it is important for Kotak? What will happen to Deutsche Bank’s customers? What does this mean for India’s banking sector?

articles.headline: Iran accelerates ceasefire proposal for US negotiations
articles.title: Trump signals progress on Iran deal as Tehran pushes faster ceasefire
articles.summary: Iranian officials stated on Monday that their seven-step ceasefire proposal submitted to the United States has been condensed for faster implementation within two days. The plan involves reopening the Strait of Hormuz and resuming nuclear talks. Discussions are ongoing with Qatari mediators, while US President Donald Trump indicated potential military action following the November 3 midterm elections if a deal is not reached.
articles.description: Iran says its offer to reopen the Strait of Hormuz can be implemented in two days if the US agrees to terms.

articles.headline: Kerala Public Service Commission faces Crime Branch probes
articles.title: Kerala PSC under the scanner: How allegations of examination irregularities have triggered multiple Crime Branch probes
articles.summary: The Kerala Public Service Commission is facing intense scrutiny following allegations of examination irregularities and evaluation lapses. A Special Investigation Team headed by Inspector General of Police S. Ajeetha Begum is currently examining multiple recruitment complaints originating from unevaluated answer sheets discovered during examinations conducted for senior posts.
articles.description: What began with the discovery of unevaluated answers in a 2023 examination for senior posts in the State Planning Board has snowballed into a wider investigation by the Crime Branch

articles.headline: Cyclone Murasu brings heavy overnight rainfall to Telangana districts
articles.title: Cyclone Murasu impact on Telangana | Extremely heavy overnight rain in Bhadradri and Khammam
articles.summary: Mandal areas in Khammam and Bhadradri Kothagudem districts recorded extremely heavy rainfall between 204 mm and 235 mm overnight due to cyclone Murasu, according to a report issued on November 4, 2026, by the Telangana Development Planning Society. The India Meteorological Department placed Bhadradri Kothagudem under an orange alert for heavy rain, while continuing showers caused accumulation reaching 88 mm in local mandals.
articles.description: Showers continue in Bhadradri Kothagudem on November 4

articles.headline: Welfare payments will use voter identity cards instead of Aadhaar according to minister
articles.title: Welfare payments will be based on voter IDs, not Aadhaar, says Panchayati Raj Minister
articles.summary: Union Minister for Panchayati Raj Rajiv Ranjan Singh stated on November 3, 2026, that welfare scheme payments will rely on voter identity cards and biometric authentication rather than Aadhaar. Speaking in Gangtok, the minister argued that the proposed shift would eliminate fraudulent entries and ensure benefits reach eligible recipients by improving the overall verification process.
articles.description: At present, welfare payments are linked to Aadhaar; Panchayati Raj Minister says people should now give EPIC number with biometrics

articles.headline: Madras High Court criticises police over political case filings
articles.title: Police must serve the State, which endures, and not the party in government, which changes: Madras High Court
articles.summary: The Madras High Court disapproved of police registering criminal cases against critics of the ruling party while granting anticipatory bail to Greater Chennai Corporation Councillor D. Sudha. Justice N. Ramesh stated that police serve the enduring State rather than changing governments. The judge also criticised the unauthorised dawn detention of Madras Institute of Development Studies Associate Professor A. Kalaiyarasan over a fake Instagram account.
articles.description: The observations were made while granting anticipatory bail to a 60-year-old Councillor, D. Sudha of the DMK, who had allegedly abused Chief Minister C. Joseph Vijay

articles.headline: Indonesia arrests former police chief over alleged illegal presidential wiretapping
articles.title: Indonesia arrests ex-police chief over alleged illegal wiretapping of President, officials
articles.summary: National police arrested former police chief Listyo Sigit Prabowo and two senior officers on November 3, 2026, for allegedly wiretapping President Prabowo Subianto and other officials without legal authorization. Presidential spokesman Prasetyo Hadi stated on November 4, 2026, that the actions could constitute treason and endanger state security, noting the President expressed profound concern over the sensitive security breach.
articles.description: ‘What was done may have fallen into the category of being considered as leading to treason,’ said a Presidential spokesperson

articles.headline: Prabowo Subianto claims victory in Indonesia presidential election
articles.title: Prabowo Subianto | The ‘reformed’ General
articles.summary: Former military general Prabowo Subianto declared victory on February 14, 2024, in Indonesia's historic three-way presidential race following unofficial counts showing a significant lead. The 72-year-old candidate transformed his public image from a strongman linked to past military brutality into a cuddly grandfather figure, successfully charming young voters during the largest one-day electoral exercise in the world.
articles.description: The former military leader and Defence Minister, who is likely to become Indonesia’s new President, was once accused of human rights abuses, but ran a campaign with a softer image of himself using Instagram and TikTok

articles.headline: Union government plans to simplify visa application forms to boost tourism
articles.title: India set to simplify visa forms
articles.summary: The Indian government plans to simplify visa application forms to meet global standards, with changes expected next year across all 22 categories. Officials stated that redundant and repetitive fields will be reduced by approximately 70% to support the travel and tourism industry. Foreign tourist arrivals reached 91.5 lakh in 2025, remaining below the 2019 pre-pandemic total of 1.093 crore.
articles.description: Redundant fields in the bulky forms will be done away with and the changes are likely to be implemented from next year, says official

articles.headline: Russian bomb attacks on Ukrainian aid centre kill 24 people
articles.title: Russian bombing of Ukrainian aid centre kills 26 people
articles.summary: Russian air strikes destroyed a school serving as a humanitarian aid center in Komyshuvakha within Ukraine's Zaporizhia region, killing 24 people. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that a repeat strike hit a shelter where residents had gathered. Regional Governor Mykhailo Semikin confirmed that casualties included two emergency rescuers and a police officer, with 27 individuals reported missing following Monday's bombardment.
articles.description: Ukraine's president calls attack further proof that Russia does not want any ‌kind of de-escalation or real justice.

articles.headline: Oil prices rise amid uncertainty over United States war with Iran
articles.title: Oil rises on Iran war uncertainty after Trump’s Republicans face election rout
articles.summary: Crude oil futures increased on November 4, 2026, during a volatile trading session as investors monitored Washington developments and ongoing conflicts. Brent futures rose 0.8 percent to $104.42 a barrel while West Texas Intermediate gained 0.5 percent to $96.59. Market sources cited an unexpected drawdown in domestic crude inventories alongside political uncertainty after Democrats captured control of the United States Congress from Republicans.
articles.description: In the previous session, Brent settled at its lowest level in nearly four weeks ‌as traders weighed talks to end the wars in Ukraine and Iran

articles.headline: The New York Times sues Brave browser for copyright infringement
articles.title: The New York Times sues Brave web browser for AI scraping and bypassing paywalls
articles.summary: The New York Times, alongside the New York Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and the Orlando Sentinel, filed lawsuits against Brave Software. The publishers accuse the web browser of unlawfully scraping copyrighted material to train artificial intelligence models and allowing users to bypass publication paywalls without permission or compensation, according to legal complaints.
articles.description: The New York Times and a group of other publications have filed lawsuits against the company that makes the Brave web browser over alleged unlawful scraping to train AI and also letting users bypass their paywalls, as reported by Reuters. According to a complaint filed by the New York Daily News, the Chicago Tribune, and […]

articles.headline: Fighting resumes in Ukraine after temporary truce near Kherson region
articles.title: Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire
articles.summary: Hostilities resumed in Ukraine's Kherson region on November 2, 2026, following a six-day ceasefire brokered by US First Lady Melania Trump. Local authorities reported fresh Russian strikes, including a hit on a medical facility in Kherson city. While the truce enabled hundreds of civilians to evacuate from Oleshky, both sides utilized the pause for military regrouping.
articles.description: Though unprecedented, the six-day truce has done little to alter the wider trajectory of a war that continues to grinds on.

articles.headline: Adani airports CEO tells foreign airlines to shift operations or stop flying
articles.title: Shift to Navi Mumbai or stop flying to Mumbai: Adani Airports CEO tells foreign airlines
articles.summary: Arun Bansal, chief executive officer of Adani Airport Holdings, stated on November 3, 2026, that international airlines unwilling to relocate to Navi Mumbai International Airport could stop flying to Mumbai. The dispute arises as Mumbai International Airport Limited prepares terminal redevelopment work, prompting carrier resistance over split operations, lack of consultation, and passenger impacts during the transition process.
articles.description: Adani Airports Holdings CEO Arun Bansal says, “Like a landlord tells its airlines to vacate his property… we have told airlines you have to vacate from April. After that where you go is your choice.”

articles.headline: US political candidates conduct final campaign events ahead of midterms
articles.title: Trump, Vance campaign with candidates on last day before US midterms
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump and Vice President JD Vance held final campaign events on November 3, 2026, ahead of the midterm elections. Republicans sought to defend congressional majorities against strong Democratic challenges driven by economic and foreign policy concerns, while a federal court reviewed a lawsuit regarding immigration agents at polling places.
articles.description: President Donald Trump closes his midterm campaign push at the Reflecting Pool, urging supporters to vote.

articles.headline: Assam Police form SIT following five murders at Guwahati hotel
articles.title: Guwahati hotel killing accused held; Assam Police announce SIT probe
articles.summary: The Assam Police established a six-member Special Investigation Team headed by Joint Commissioner Ankur Jain to investigate the killing of five people at a Guwahati hotel on October 26, 2026. Suspect Ghanakanta Gogoi was arrested shortly after the incident, which police stated stemmed from a dispute over the property lease and management.
articles.description: Police said the accused, Ghanakanta Gogoi, had inked a lease agreement with hotel owners in September 2025, and a dispute on the issue had led to the incident

articles.headline: Five people killed in shooting incident at Guwahati hotel
articles.title: Five shot dead in Guwahati hotel
articles.summary: Five individuals, including property owner Helena Bharali and her son Debarshi Bharali, were killed in a shooting at a hotel in the Ulubari area of Guwahati on October 26, 2026. Another person sustained injuries and received treatment at the Gauhati Medical College and Hospital. Local authorities apprehended a suspect following the violent episode.
articles.description: The victims include a mother-son duo; police nab one suspect

articles.headline: Iran offers to reopen Hormuz strait within two days if US agrees
articles.title: Iran says ready to reopen Hormuz in two days if U.S. agrees to demands
articles.summary: Tehran announced readiness to reopen the strategic Strait of Hormuz within forty-eight hours if Washington accepts specific conditions, including lifting oil sanctions and ending military actions. Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei stated on November 2, 2026, that messages are being exchanged through mediators while U.S. President Donald Trump simultaneously issued renewed threats during election campaigning.
articles.description: A senior Iranian official said the offer to open the vital energy corridor, which follows intense efforts by mediators to stop a return to war, showed good faith

articles.headline: Supreme Court orders time-bound financial aid and rehabilitation for freed bonded labourers
articles.title: Supreme Court orders time-bound financial aid, rehabilitation for rescued bonded labourers
articles.summary: The Supreme Court directed the Centre on November 2, 2026, to ensure financial assistance is disbursed to rescued bonded labourers within seven days of release. A Bench of Justices Vikram Nath and Aparesh Kumar Singh instructed States and Union Territories to implement a revised standard operating procedure within six months, aiming to eradicate institutional shortcomings, strengthen inter-state coordination, and secure meaningful rehabilitation.
articles.description: Bench says eradication of bonded labour is a “continuing obligation”, requiring authorities to ensure that those freed are meaningfully rehabilitated

articles.headline: Spoiled by design: How supermarkets became targets of cyberattacks
articles.title: Spoiled by design: How supermarkets became targets of cyberattacks
articles.description: Outlets of Carrefour, Spar and Delhaize were hit, and even a few restaurants run by furniture maker Ikea

articles.headline: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel dies following collision with goalkeeper
articles.title: Spanish footballer dies after collision with keeper
articles.summary: Tenerife striker Jesus de Miguel passed away on November 3, 2026, after suffering injuries from a collision with FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono during a second division match at Heliodoro Rodriguez Lopez stadium. Spanish police launched an investigation into the incident, which occurred with the score tied 2-2. The player experienced a cardiac arrest and subsequent neurological worsening before his death, prompting widespread tributes across the Spanish football community.
articles.description: ‘Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe this is real, CD Tenerife announces the tragic death, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda,’ his club Tenerife said in a statement.

articles.headline: Odisha government expedites evacuation of vulnerable areas as Cyclone Murasu approaches
articles.title: Odisha braces for severe cyclonic storm Murasu, evacuates 1.6 lakh people
articles.summary: The Odisha government accelerated evacuations from vulnerable areas on Monday as Cyclone Murasu strengthened into a severe storm in the Bay of Bengal. Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari stated that over 300 rescue teams have been pre-positioned across southern districts like Ganjam and Gajapati, where the India Meteorological Department forecast heavy rainfall and gusty winds reaching up to 50 kmph.
articles.description: The State government’s preparedness efforts are focused on the five districts of Ganjam, Gajapati, Malkangiri, Koraput, and Kandhamal

articles.headline: Keralam orders vigilance examination of bribery allegations against CEC
articles.title: Keralam Home Minister directs Vigilance to examine ₹2-crore bribery allegation against CEC Gyanesh Kumar
articles.summary: Keralam Home Minister Ramesh Chennithala instructed the Vigilance and Anti-Corruption Bureau to examine new bribery allegations against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar. A former contractor alleged that Kumar demanded a two-crore-rupee bribe regarding a road project two decades ago when Kumar served as Public Works Department Secretary.
articles.description: Charges in connection with a road construction project undertaken under Kerala State Transport Project nearly two decades ago when the current CEC was serving as PWD Secretary in Keralam

articles.headline: Union Health Ministry proposes ten new import gateways
articles.title: Centre proposes 10 new import gateways for drugs, medical devices
articles.summary: The Union Health Ministry has proposed amending Rule 43A of the Drugs Rules of 1945 to add 10 inland container depots, a Special Economic Zone, and Noida International Airport as authorised entry points for importing drugs, medical devices, and cosmetics. According to the ministry, this expansion aims to reduce inland transportation distances, optimise logistics costs, and improve supply chain efficiency across India.
articles.description: The proposed amendment to Rule 43A of the Drugs Rules, 1945, is aimed at easing import operations, reducing inland transportation distances and improving the movement of healthcare products across the country

articles.headline: India boosts regional navigation capabilities with successful NVS-03 satellite launch
articles.title: What is the debate on NavIC vs GPS | Explained
articles.summary: India strengthened its regional satellite-based navigation system known as NavIC by successfully deploying the NVS-03 satellite in late October 2026. The Indian Space Research Organisation stated that the new satellite operates across multiple frequency bands and features both indigenous and imported atomic clocks, renewing discussions regarding domestic navigation systems versus GPS.
articles.description: From a strategic perspective, the argument is quite straightforward given the origins of the IRNSS concept in the aftermath of the U.S.’s denial of its Global Positioning Service (GPS) during the 1999 Kargil conflict

articles.headline: Business jet crash in Florida claims lives of nine people
articles.title: Jet crashes into South Florida neighbourhood, killing all nine on board and leaving a fiery crater
articles.summary: A Learjet 60 business jet crashed into a residential neighborhood in South Florida on November 1, 2026, resulting in the deaths of all nine individuals on board, according to United States Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy. The aircraft, bearing tail number N722BD, had departed from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was traveling toward the Bahamas before plunging near Military Trail and 10th Avenue North.
articles.description: The aircraft had departed Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas and was headed to the Bahamas, according to the Federal Aviation Administration

articles.headline: Audit highlights heavy drinking water financial burden on poor Bengaluru families
articles.title: Bengaluru families pay ₹3,000 per month for water, reveals survey by volunteers
articles.summary: Economically weaker families in Bengaluru spend around 3,000 rupees monthly on private water tankers due to an impending drinking water crisis caused by a monsoon deficit, according to preliminary water audit findings by the Water Satyagraha campaign. Campaign convenor Syed Ahmed Hussain stated that poor households spend more on water than the state government's monthly assistance, while the city faces a projected shortfall exceeding 600 million litres daily.
articles.description: The city extracts groundwater at nearly twice the rate at which it is replenished and loses about 400 million litres of piped water every day, according to Syed Ahmed Hussain, convenor of the Water Satyagraha campaign

articles.headline: Israeli strikes kill three Palestinians in Gaza Strip, health officials report
articles.title: Israeli strikes kill three people in Gaza, medics say
articles.summary: Israeli airstrikes killed at least three Palestinians and wounded several others across the Gaza Strip on November 2, 2026, according to territory health officials. Medics reported two deaths in Khan Younis and one in Al-Mussadar. The Israeli military stated the strikes targeted militants, while ongoing conflict and stalled ceasefire negotiations continue to affect more than two million residents.
articles.description: Medics said two people were ⁠killed and six others wounded in two separate airstrikes in Khan Younis while ‌a third person was killed in an Israeli airstrike in the town of ‌Al-Mussadar

articles.headline: Prime accused in Guwahati hotel shooting killed in Sivasagar police encounter
articles.title: Guwahati hotel shooting case: Prime accused killed in police ‘encounter’
articles.summary: The prime suspect in an October 26 hotel shooting in Guwahati that left five people dead was shot dead during an alleged police encounter in Sivasagar on November 4, 2026. According to senior police officials, 34-year-old Ghanakanta Gogoi attacked officers and attempted to escape while being transported in connection with a separate bank fraud case.
articles.description: The police were taking Ghanakanta Gogoi to eastern Assam’s Sivasagar in connection with a 2024 bank fraud case

articles.headline: Delhi Police chief tells Supreme Court that Jantar Mantar is public road
articles.title: Jantar Mantar is a road, not a site, says Delhi Police chief
articles.summary: Delhi Police Commissioner Anurag Kumar submitted an affidavit to the Supreme Court on November 3, 2026, stating that Jantar Mantar is a public road rather than a designated protest site. He argued that continuous demonstrations create severe security risks, disrupt emergency services, and infringe upon the rights of local residents and businesses.
articles.description: In an affidavit in the Supreme Court, Delhi Police Commissioner says none can insist on a right to protest only at a specific site and the State has power to change venue

articles.headline: Prime Minister Narendra Modi to inaugurate Bengaluru metro Pink Line on November 13
articles.title: It’s official: Bengaluru’s Pink Line to be inaugurated on November 13
articles.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the elevated section of the Pink Line of the Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Ltd. on November 13, 2026, according to Greater Bengaluru Development Minister Krishna Byre Gowda. The launch will push the operational network past 100 km, as authorities aim for 170 km by 2027 to expand public transport.
articles.description: The inauguration would take the operational metro network in Bengaluru beyond 100 km, marking a significant expansion of the city’s public transport infrastructure

articles.headline: CITU announces indefinite protest at Jantar Mantar in Delhi
articles.title: Over one lakh workers expected at Jantar Mantar in Delhi for indefinite protest by CITU starting December 1
articles.summary: The Centre of Indian Trade Unions will launch an indefinite protest at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi on December 1, 2026, demanding the repeal of labour codes and the protection of workers' rights. CITU State unit president S. Varalakshmi stated that over one lakh workers are expected to participate, highlighting concerns over unorganised sector wages, safety, and rising worker suicides.
articles.description: The Centre of Indian Trade Unions (CITU) will launch an indefinite protest at Jantar Mantar demanding protection of workers’ rights and repeal of ‘anti-worker’ labour codes

articles.headline: China ramps up Middle East diplomacy with high-level meetings involving Iran and Oman
articles.title: China steps up Middle East diplomacy with Iran and Oman meetings
articles.summary: Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with an Iranian security official in Beijing on November 2, 2026, while President Xi Jinping hosted Oman’s Sultan Haitham bin Tariq. Beijing renewed calls for dialogue regarding the conflict and signed fourteen cooperation documents with Oman. Officials emphasized the importance of safeguarding energy routes and called for the resumption of safe navigation through the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.description: Beijing urges dialogue on US-Iran war, sends envoy to Gulf as Xi hosts first Omani head of state visit since 1978.

articles.headline: WHO warns northern Ethiopian conflict threatens health system with collapse
articles.title: Violence in northern Ethiopia pushing health system towards collapse: WHO
articles.summary: Escalating fighting and drone strikes in northern Ethiopia are driving the regional medical infrastructure toward total collapse, according to World Health Organization Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus. Speaking on November 2, 2026, Tedros reported that recent violence has killed multiple civilians, including children in the Amhara region, while severe shortages of staff, medicine, and ambulances hinder life-saving care.
articles.description: Renewed fighting between rebels from northern Tigray and ​the government in Addis Ababa has shattered 2022 peace deal.

articles.headline: Nervous Republicans await results at Paxton’s Texas election party
articles.title: Nervous Republicans await results at Paxton’s Texas election party
articles.description: Texas Republicans are anxiously waiting to see if the state’s attorney general can hold off his Democrat challenger.

articles.headline: Chinese embassy claims object found in Papua New Guinea is wine bottle
articles.title: Weapon or wine bottle? China disputes reports of artillery shell in Papua New Guinea
articles.summary: Chinese authorities rejected reports that a military artillery shell was discovered inside a commercial shipping container in Papua New Guinea, claiming the 32kg object is actually a wine bottle. Local police previously arrested four Chinese nationals after finding the device at a construction site in Port Moresby, prompting an ongoing security investigation.
articles.description: Papua New Guinea police had earlier dismissed speculation that the 32kg object was "merely a dummy".

articles.headline: Government issues new rules allowing airfare intervention in extraordinary situations
articles.title: Centre can intervene on airfares in ‘extraordinary’ circumstances, new rules say
articles.summary: Under newly framed rules notified on October 31, the Union government can now issue written directions to airlines regarding ticket prices during extraordinary situations. The regulations require carriers to submit tariffs to the Director General of Civil Aviation and publish detailed cost breakdowns on digital platforms. While providing for enhanced price monitoring, authorities maintained that base fares remain market-driven without direct caps.
articles.description: Centre has previously imposed fare bands during the pandemic, IndiGo’s operational breakdown, and urged restraint during disasters, festivities; new rules also mandate closer monitoring of fares by DGCA

articles.headline: Amit Shah challenges Rahul Gandhi to debate parliamentary session on electoral rolls
articles.title: Amit Shah dares Rahul Gandhi to debate SIR issue, says government is ready to convene special session of Parliament
articles.summary: Union Home Minister Amit Shah challenged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to a debate during a special session of Parliament on Monday. Dismissing opposition allegations regarding electronic voting machines and voter rolls, Shah asserted that the government is fully prepared to convene the House. He also strongly criticized opposition rallies and vowed that authorities would systematically remove every infiltrator from electoral rolls.
articles.description: If a Parliament session is held, Prime Minister Narendra Modi will shred Congress into pieces, Amit Shah said

articles.headline: Al Jazeera condemns extension of Israeli operational ban and calls for immediate lifting
articles.title: Al Jazeera condemns Israeli ban extension, calls for its immediate lifting
articles.summary: The Qatar-based Al Jazeera Media Network strongly condemned the Tel Aviv court decision approving a ninety-day extension of its operational ban in Israel. Calling the measure an assault on press freedom, the organization rejected allegations used to justify the restrictions and criticized the lack of due process regarding secret material. The network announced it is reviewing the ruling with legal counsel to protect its journalists and public access to information.
articles.description: Network calls move 'assault' on press freedom, warns of 'dangerous pattern' that undermines ability to report facts.

articles.headline: Jon Ossoff wins Senate reelection in Georgia
articles.title: Rising Democratic star Jon Ossoff’s reelection fuels presidential prospects
articles.summary: Democratic Senator Jon Ossoff won reelection to the United States Senate in Georgia on November 3, 2026, defeating Republican challenger Mike Collins. NBC News and CBS News called the race for the 39-year-old lawmaker, whose victory further elevates his national profile within the Democratic Party. In his victory speech, Mr. Ossoff stated that the midterm results represented a clear rejection of President Donald Trump by American voters.
articles.description: While the 39-year-old has said that he has “zero interest in running for President,” his victory in Georgia bolsters his status in the Democratic Party two years before the next presidential vote

articles.headline: Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats
articles.title: Seven flights across Europe targeted by suspected bomb threats
articles.description: Seven flights across Europe were targeted by suspected bomb threats.

articles.headline: US oil firms earn over $130bn in profits during war on Iran
articles.title: How US oil firms profit $130bn from Iran war as household bills surge
articles.summary: United States oil companies earned more than 130 billion dollars in profits during the war on Iran, according to The New York Times, while consumers faced soaring costs. Brown University reported that Americans spent an extra 150 billion dollars on petrol and diesel. Analysts warned that high energy prices could risk economic growth and potential recession while increasing shareholder returns.
articles.description: As energy from the Gulf and Russia take a hit, American oil and gas firms are the big gainers.

articles.headline: Suhas Subramanyam wins re-election in Virginia congressional district
articles.title: Suhas Subramanyam re-elected as U.S. Congressman from Virginia
articles.summary: Suhas Subramanyam secured re-election to the United States House of Representatives representing Virginia’s 10th congressional district. Subramanyam polled over 61.5 percent of the vote against Republican challenger Dave Beckwith, who received 36.4 percent of the ballots cast. The 40-year-old former White House technology policy advisor to President Barack Obama previously served in the Virginia General Assembly and state senate.
articles.description: Mr. Subramanyam, 40, won from Virginia’s 10th congressional district, polling over 61.5% of the vote against Republican Dave Beckwith, who managed to win 36.4% of the ballots cast

articles.headline: Israel's policy aims to minimize Palestinian population, says UN official
articles.title: Israel’s intent is to prevent Palestinians from existing as a group: Justice Muralidhar
articles.summary: Israel implements policies to maximize the occupation of Palestinian territories and minimize the Palestinian population, according to Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar. Speaking on a podcast, the chair of the UN-appointed Independent International Commission of Inquiry stated the commission demonstrated Israel's intent to prevent Palestinians from existing as a group while gathering evidence of war crimes in occupied territories.
articles.description: In a strong indictment of Israel’s policies in the occupied Palestinian territories, Justice Srinivasan Muralidhar, chair of the UN-appointed Independent International Commission of Inquiry, has accused Israel of seeking to expand its occupation while reducing the Palestinian population

articles.headline: Iran military warns third conflict with US and Israel will be costly
articles.title: How would Tehran respond if the US and Israel bomb Iran again?
articles.summary: Iran military officials warned that a renewed war with the United States and Israel would be longer and more costly than expected, utilizing new weapons and asymmetric warfare. Former Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps commander Hossein Kanani Moghaddam said Iranian forces are in better operational shape, while analysts noted ongoing domestic security concerns and intelligence weaknesses within the regime.
articles.description: Iran has retained significant offensive capability, but civilians and critical infrastructure remain largely exposed.

articles.headline: Ballot shortages reported in Dearborn, Michigan
articles.title: Ballot shortages reported in Dearborn, Michigan
articles.description: Reports of ballot shortages at several Dearborn polling stations have raised concerns over voter access

articles.headline: India monitors garment worker protests in Bangladesh following factory closures
articles.title: ‘Following situation’: MEA on protests by garment workers in Bangladesh
articles.summary: India stated on November 3, 2026, that it is closely following the situation regarding garment worker protests in Bangladesh over pay demands. The unrest has forced hundreds of factories to shut down in Dhaka, Gazipur, and Mymensingh. External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal also addressed bilateral ties and the expiring Ganga Water Treaty.
articles.description: The garment workers are holding protests over their demand for higher pay, prompting authorities to deploy additional paramilitary forces after reports surfaced of vandalism and violence

articles.headline: French students blockade schools and universities demanding education reforms
articles.title: Students blockade dozens of French schools and universities
articles.summary: Students across France blockaded dozens of high schools and universities on November 3, 2026, to protest against education policies and demand increased funding. Authorities reported disruptions at numerous institutions amidst tight security and nationwide protests, while Education Minister Edouard Geffray condemned the actions for depriving students of their fundamental right to an education.
articles.description: After returning from a two-week autumn break, some students resumed their protest campaign on November 2

articles.headline: Spain transport minister resigns after deadly train crash kills 69 people
articles.title: Spain’s Transport Minister offers resignation after deadly train crash
articles.summary: Spain's Transport Minister Oscar Puente resigned on November 3, 2026, and withdrew from an upcoming election following a railway disaster near Madrid that killed 69 people. The crash involved a Renfe train colliding with an Iryo service. Puente announced financial aid for families and new safety software measures to reduce human error.
articles.description: Last week's crash, along with another disaster earlier this year, has overshadowed the campaign for the ballot, with PM Sanchez trailing in opinion polls

articles.headline: United Nations elects five new judges to International Court of Justice
articles.title: UN elects five judges to International Court of Justice amid record cases
articles.summary: The United Nations elected five new judges on Tuesday to nine-year terms on the International Court of Justice, which currently faces a record caseload. The newly elected panel members are from the United Kingdom, France, Jordan, Singapore, and Kenya. Their terms begin on February 6, 2027, as the court handles multiple international disputes and genocide cases.
articles.description: The election, held at UN headquarters, required several rounds of voting to fill the fifth and final seat.

articles.headline: Iran says US talks could resume ‘within a short period’ if demands are met
articles.title: Iran says US talks could resume ‘within a short period’ if demands are met
articles.description: Esmaeil Baghaei said Qatar is facilitating indirect talks based on Iran’s seven-step peace plan.

articles.headline: FBI arrests Oklahoma man for mailing hundreds of threatening letters
articles.title: FBI arrests man for sending over 700 threatening letters to US officials
articles.summary: Robin Patrick Martin appeared in a United States district court after federal agents arrested him for allegedly mailing over seven hundred threatening letters containing nonhazardous white powder to officials and pollsters. Prosecutors stated the Oklahoma City man expressed grievances regarding the 2020 election. The Federal Bureau of Investigation utilized video footage and fingerprints to link Martin to the mailings.
articles.description: The suspect, an Oklahoma City man, is accused of mailing hoax letters with white powder and treason warnings.

articles.headline: Nexus Mods mandates artificial intelligence disclosures for new uploads
articles.title: The biggest modding site in PC gaming is taking a stance on AI
articles.summary: PC gaming platform Nexus Mods announced that authors uploading new modifications must declare whether artificial intelligence was utilized in their creation. Site owner Victor Folmann stated the platform avoids an outright ban to maintain transparency, requiring public explanations for assisted content. Authors have a sixty-day grace period ending on January second to update existing modifications.
articles.description: The PC gaming mods repository Nexus Mods is making disclosures about AI mandatory for uploads of new mods, meaning that mod authors will have to declare "whether AI has been used in their work," the site announced today as part of a big post about AI-generated content on the platform. "One of the most consistent […]

articles.headline: Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe with no explosive devices found
articles.title: Bomb threats disrupt flights across Europe, no explosive devices found
articles.summary: Multiple passenger flights and an Israel-bound cruise ship faced bomb threats across Europe on Tuesday, prompting emergency security checks and flight diversions in Poland, Italy, Spain, and Bulgaria. Authorities confirmed that all inspections yielded negative results and no explosives were discovered. The incidents follow similar disruptions earlier in the week, amid ongoing concerns regarding hybrid attacks and sabotage across the continent.
articles.description: At least seven flights and an Israel-bound cruise ship received threats, but officials say searches found no explosives.

articles.headline: IPS officer Anurag Sujania resigns after transfer following hooch tragedies
articles.title: Days after transfer as Sagar SP, IPS officer Anurag Sujania resigns amid ongoing liquor row in M.P.
articles.summary: Indian Police Service officer Anurag Sujania resigned from his position citing personal reasons following his transfer from the Sagar Superintendent of Police post. The bureaucratic reshuffle occurred in late October after more than twenty five people died in a district hooch tragedy. Police sources indicated he was upset over the transfer, while the state government faces mounting pressure regarding multiple illicit alcohol incidents.
articles.description: Anurag Sujania, along with Sagar Collector Pratibha Pal, had been removed on October 27, over a month after a hooch tragedy killed more than 25 in the district

articles.headline: Driver who ran over police officer arrested after police encounter
articles.title: Driver who ran over M.P. police officer arrested
articles.summary: Gajendra Rawat was arrested in Alirajpur district for allegedly running over Khategaon police station in charge Dilip Puri, who died during a vehicle check involving illicit liquor. The suspect suffered a leg injury during a subsequent police encounter while being transported to Dewas. Authorities have also apprehended several other individuals linked to an interstate bootlegging network operating between Harda and Gujarat.
articles.description: Special DG Upendra Jain told The Hindu that while arresting the driver is a priority, various teams are also looking for the other three accused of an interstate illicit liquor racket

articles.headline: Ballot scanner glitch disrupts voting in New York
articles.title: Ballot scanner glitch disrupts voting in New York
articles.description: There have been voting machine scanner failures at polling sites 50 km north of New York City

articles.headline: Technical issues delay voting at polling locations across United States
articles.title: Where have there been technical issues so far during US midterm elections?
articles.summary: Technical malfunctions affected several polling locations across the United States during the midterm elections, prompting officials to extend voting hours. In Westchester County, New York, thick ballot paper caused problems for automatic reading machines made by Liberty Vote, requiring manual counts with police escorts. Similar operational hurdles, machine setup issues, and temporary power outages were reported in Florida, North Carolina, Arizona, and Pennsylvania.
articles.description: Some polling stations have experienced vote-delaying issues that officials describe as being minor.

articles.headline: Wall Street leaders divided over artificial intelligence market risks
articles.title: Please stop asking me when the AI bubble will pop
articles.summary: Wall Street executives and major financial managers expressed conflicting views regarding artificial intelligence market risks during the 2026 Global Financial Leaders Investment Summit in Hong Kong. Pacific Investment Management Company Chief Executive Officer Emmanuel Roman warned of an impending market downturn as expensive infrastructure demands strain debt markets. Meanwhile, major technology firms continue raising billions through bond offerings to fund extensive artificial intelligence buildouts.
articles.description: People, including on this staff, keep asking me with varying degrees of excitement or trepidation when the AI bubble will burst. I'll tell you what I tell them: If I knew that, I would make a life-changing bet on the market, levered up as far as I could, and then, after I made my money, […]

articles.headline: India manufacturing sector activity growth eases in October amid softer output and new orders
articles.title: Manufacturing PMI eases to 54.7 in October, but overseas demand at six-month high
articles.summary: India's manufacturing sector growth slowed in October as output and new orders increased at milder rates, according to the HSBC India Manufacturing Purchasing Managers' Index compiled by S&P Global. The seasonally adjusted index fell to 54.7 from 55.1 in September.
